title: Росія атакувала Львів і Івано-Франківськ, у Києві, Ірпені та Кривому Розі загиблі після балістичного удару, пошкоджене метро і лікарня
content_c:
Росія атакувала Львів і Івано-Франківськ, у Києві, Ірпені та Кривому Розі загиблі після балістичного удару, пошкоджене метро і лікарня
  - Author, Відділ новин
  - Role, ВВС News Україна
- Published
- Час прочитання: 5 хв
Зранку 19 жовтня Росія атакувала реактивним шахедом Львів та Івано-Франківськ, від обстрілу балістикою ввечері напередодні та вночі проти 19 жовтня у Києві загинула 21-літня дівчина, є поранені. Також столицю вночі атакували шахеди. Повідомляють про великі руйнування у Ірпені під Києвом від балістики, там є загибла людина. Двоє людей загинули від удару по Кривому Розі.
Джерело ВВС в офісі президента вказує, що під час першої хвилі балістичного удару по Києву знову не було попередження від США. Проблеми з обміном розвідувальними даними тривають від дизельної угоди Трампа і Путіна та вимогою США не бити по НПЗ Росії.
"Цієї ночі було два балістичні удари: один – о 23:00, другий – о третій годині ночі. Про перший попереджень від США не було", – повідомив речник Повітряних сил Юрій Ігнат.
Згодом Володимир Зеленський додав деталей про обстріл.
"Знову російська балістична атака кількома хвилями за ніч, і знову не було попередження від партнерів. Знову мішенню були енергетика та інфраструктура, але пошкоджені також медична клініка, школа, станція метро та звичайні житлові будинки. Загалом росіяни застосували 16 балістичних ракет, і це була цілеспрямована атака проти Києва та Київщини".
Він каже, що атакували 28 підстанцій та енергетичних об'єктів.
Через дефіцит протиракет до системи PATRIOT жодної балістичної ракети не збили.
Зранку 19 жовтня дронова атака триває майже по всій Україні.
Годину літав біля Львова і удар по Франківську
Про наближення дрона до Львова написали керівник міста Андрій Садовий та області Максим Козицький.
За даними моніторів, дрон залетів у місто, а далі кружляв над його околицями щонайменше п'ять разів. Повідомляли про роботу ППО.
Згодом Козицький вказав, що дрон полетів у бік Волині й у місті скасували тривогу. Але о 8.40 дрон повернувся, у передмісті Львова його збили.
"У селі Зубра Львівського району, за інформацією на цю годину, пошкоджені 11 житлових будинків та 8 автівок. Попередньо, близько 08:50 наші воїни ППО збили ворожий безпілотник, уламки впали на приватну територію", - повідомив Козицький. Поранених немає.
Моніторингові канали припускали, що це міг бути розвідувальний дрон без бойової частини.
Напередодні дрони також атакували Львів. В околицях збили два дрони, пошкоджені житлові будинки, горів логістичний склад.
Після 11.20 реактивний дрон атакував Івано-Франківськ, про роботу ППО містян попередив мер Руслан Марцінків.
Удар балістикою по Києву
Пізно ввечері 18 жовтня та вночі проти 19 жовтня Росія кілька разів атакувала балістичними ракетами столицю і передмістя.
Спочатку мер Віталій Кличко повідомив про загиблу дівчину віком 21 рік. Потім він додав інформацію про 8 поранених.
Пошкоджений 25-поверховий будинок.
Станція метро "Чернігівська" отримала ушкодження, ця лінія зранку працює зі змінами.
Метрополітен вказує, що внаслідок масованого обстрілу столиці пошкоджена наземна станція метрополітену, а також колії та кабельну мережу
Вранці рух поїздів розпочався між станціями "Академмістечко" – "Дарниця" згідно з графіком.
Наземні станції "Чернігівська" та "Лісова" тимчасово будуть зачинені на вхід і вихід.
ДСНС вказала, що у ніч проти 19 жовтня Росія завдала балістичних ударів по столиці. Наслідки зафіксовані щонайменше у трьох районах міста.
У Деснянському районі горіла нежитлова будівля, пошкоджено автомобілі та станцію метро. На місці пожежі виявили загиблу людину.
У Солом'янському районі виникла пожежа у приміщенні медичного закладу, пошкоджено фасад і скління багатоповерхівки.
У Дніпровському районі пошкоджений заклад освіти - льодова арена "Шалетт".
Через атаку балістики у Києві повністю виведені з ладу обладнання та інфраструктура датаценту "Датагруп". Це всеукраїнський постачальник послуг зв'язку.
"На жаль, його відновлення та подальша робота неможливі. Наші співробітники не постраждали. Продовжуємо надавати сервіси клієнтам із резервних майданчиків", - написали в компанії.
Також росіяни атакували виробничі потужності заводу "Планета Пластик", який спеціалізується на виробництві пластикової продукції.
Після повного знищення підприємства у 2022 році компанія побудувала нове. Його відкрили у вересні 2025 року. 31 серпня 2026 року завод оголошував про зупинку роботи через безпекову ситуацію.
Зранку Кличко повідомив, що у Соломʼянському районі значних ушкоджень зазнав один із Консультативно-діагностичних центрів міста. Вибуховою хвилею вибило понад 200 вікон, двері в приміщеннях, пошкодило стелі. А також обладнання в медзакладі.
Постраждалих серед персоналу немає. Пацієнтів на момент атаки в медичному центрі не було.
Руйнування в Ірпені
Влада Ірпеня під Києвом також повідомила про великі руйнування та пожежі від удару балістикою. Від прямого влучання ракети в будинок є загибла людина.
"Внаслідок прямого влучання по приватному сектору загинула жінка", - повідомив перший заступник Ірпінського міського голови Олександр Пащинський.
Голова Київської обласної державної адміністрації Тимур Ткаченко згодом написав, що в Ірпені травмовано шестеро людей, серед них - троє дітей.
"Ще троє людей зникли безвісти. Наразі тривають пошуки", - сказав Ткаченко. У його повідомленні немає інформації про загиблу.
Проте згодом ДСНС підтвердила загиблу людину і трьох зниклих.
Ткаченко також уточнив, шо в Бучанському районі пошкоджені 11 приватних будинків, 6 автомобілів, виробниче та складське приміщення, заклад освіти. У багатоквартирних житлових будинках вибиті вікна.
У Вишгородському районі пошкодили приватний будинок, 5 автомобілів та об'єкт інфраструктури.
Кривий Ріг
19 жовтня російські війська атакували промислове підприємство в Покровському районі Кривого Рогу, внаслідок чого загинули двоє чоловіків, ще семеро людей дістали поранення, серед них – 15-річний хлопець.
Керівник міста Олександр Вілкул завияв, що росіяни завдали удару "Бандероллю". Дані про сімох поранених він оприлюднив станом на 12:30. Раніше він повідомляв про трьох, а згодом – чотирьох постраждалих.
Також унаслідок атаки пошкоджено 17 багатоповерхових будинків: вибито майже 50 вікон, пошкоджено три покрівлі. Також постраждали промислове підприємство, пошта, банк, коледж, магазини та автівки.
description: Росія завдала комбінованого удару по Україні, застосувавши балістичні ракети та ударні дрони. Внаслідок атак є загиблі та поранені, зафіксовані руйнування в Києві, на Київщині та Львівщині.

  - Author, Відділ новин
  - Role, ВВС News Україна
- Published
- Час прочитання: 5 хв
Зранку 19 жовтня Росія атакувала реактивним шахедом Львів та Івано-Франківськ, від обстрілу балістикою ввечері напередодні та вночі проти 19 жовтня у Києві загинула 21-літня дівчина, є поранені. Також столицю вночі атакували шахеди. Повідомляють про великі руйнування у Ірпені під Києвом від балістики, там є загибла людина. Двоє людей загинули від удару по Кривому Розі.
Джерело ВВС в офісі президента вказує, що під час першої хвилі балістичного удару по Києву знову не було попередження від США. Проблеми з обміном розвідувальними даними тривають від дизельної угоди Трампа і Путіна та вимогою США не бити по НПЗ Росії.
"Цієї ночі було два балістичні удари: один – о 23:00, другий – о третій годині ночі. Про перший попереджень від США не було", – повідомив речник Повітряних сил Юрій Ігнат.
Згодом Володимир Зеленський додав деталей про обстріл.
"Знову російська балістична атака кількома хвилями за ніч, і знову не було попередження від партнерів. Знову мішенню були енергетика та інфраструктура, але пошкоджені також медична клініка, школа, станція метро та звичайні житлові будинки. Загалом росіяни застосували 16 балістичних ракет, і це була цілеспрямована атака проти Києва та Київщини".
Він каже, що атакували 28 підстанцій та енергетичних об'єктів.
Через дефіцит протиракет до системи PATRIOT жодної балістичної ракети не збили.
Зранку 19 жовтня дронова атака триває майже по всій Україні.
Годину літав біля Львова і удар по Франківську
Про наближення дрона до Львова написали керівник міста Андрій Садовий та області Максим Козицький.
За даними моніторів, дрон залетів у місто, а далі кружляв над його околицями щонайменше п'ять разів. Повідомляли про роботу ППО.
Згодом Козицький вказав, що дрон полетів у бік Волині й у місті скасували тривогу. Але о 8.40 дрон повернувся, у передмісті Львова його збили.
"У селі Зубра Львівського району, за інформацією на цю годину, пошкоджені 11 житлових будинків та 8 автівок. Попередньо, близько 08:50 наші воїни ППО збили ворожий безпілотник, уламки впали на приватну територію", - повідомив Козицький. Поранених немає.
Моніторингові канали припускали, що це міг бути розвідувальний дрон без бойової частини.
Напередодні дрони також атакували Львів. В околицях збили два дрони, пошкоджені житлові будинки, горів логістичний склад.
Після 11.20 реактивний дрон атакував Івано-Франківськ, про роботу ППО містян попередив мер Руслан Марцінків.

Пізно ввечері 18 жовтня та вночі проти 19 жовтня Росія кілька разів атакувала балістичними ракетами столицю і передмістя.

title: Окупанти за добу втратили 1560 осіб та 1578 БпЛА – Генштаб
content_c:
Сили оборони України за добу ліквідували 1560 окупантів, 42 артилерійські системи, 5 бронемашин, 1578 БпЛА, а також 293 авто та чотири одиниці спецтехніки, інформує Генеральний штаб Збройних сил України у своєму ранковому зведенні у Телеграм.
"Загальні бойові втрати противника з 24.02.22 по 20.10.26 склали: особового складу – близько 1 568 720 (+1560) осіб, танків – 12 425 (+9); бойових броньованих машин – 25 570 (+5); артилерійських систем – 51 359 (42); РСЗВ – 2 227 (+3); засоби ППО – 1 714 (+0); літаків – 449 (+0); гелікоптерів – 356 (+0); наземних робототехнічних комплексів – 2 986 (+12); БПЛА оперативно-тактичного рівня – 571 572 (+1578); крилаті ракети – 5 138 (+4); кораблі/катери – 35 (+0); підводні човни – 2 (+0); автомобільна техніка та автоцистерни – 164 871 (+293); спеціальна техніка – 4 842 (+4)", – йдеться у повідомленні.

title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon
content_c:
Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon
- Published
A spacecraft has launched from Japan headed for Mars' moon Phobos, where it will attempt to grab some moondust and bring it back to Earth.
If it is successful, this will become the first time a sample has been returned from Mars or its moons to be analysed in laboratories here on Earth.
The spacecraft is scheduled to arrive at Phobos in August 2027.
It is hoped that the Mars Moons Exploration (MMX) mission, which is led by the Japanese Space Agency, will solve the mystery of how Mars's moons formed.
Prof Sara Russell, from the Natural History Museum, who is the MMX mission's deputy for sample analysis, said: "There hasn't yet been a successful mission to go to Phobos and bring a bit back to Earth.
"I think this is an incredibly ambitious and fun mission," she said.
There are only three moons in the inner Solar System: our own Moon, and two around Mars, which are called Phobos and Deimos.
Both of these are tiny - Phobos is about 20km (12 miles) across and Deimos is about 10km (six miles) across. They are also irregularly shaped, looking a bit like space potatoes.
The MMX spacecraft will study Deimos as it arrives in the Mars neighbourhood, and then will focus on Phobos.
It plans to set down a small rover to explore the terrain, though this will be no easy feat.
Sara Russell says no one has ever landed a rover on such a small moon.
"The moon itself doesn't have very much of its own gravity," she explained.
"But it's next to an enormous planet that's got a much higher gravity, and that makes it much harder to get a rover onto the surface."
The rover will scout out a landing site so that the MMX spacecraft itself can later touch down on Phobos.
Once on the surface, it will deploy a robotic arm and two samplers to grab some moon dust.
This material will be packed into a small capsule that will return to Earth in 2031, landing in the Woomera desert of South Australia.
The amount of material that will come back is tiny - just 10g.
"It's a very small [amount] actually," said Dr Chrysa Avdellidou, from Leicester University, who is working with the Japanese mission.
"However we can do several studies even on individual grains… You don't need to have kilos back from a surface in order to do science. So it's worth every gram," she said.
Scientists believe the sample will finally shed light on the puzzle of where Mars's moons came from.
There are two competing ideas.
Either a space rock smashed into Mars early in its history, and Phobos and Deimos were created from the debris.
Or the moons are two wandering asteroids from the outer Solar System, which were grabbed by the Red Planet's gravity.
"When we get the sample back, we'll be able to look in detail at its chemistry and its mineral composition - and the two hypotheses will produce very distinct results," said Sara Russell.
"It should be pretty much immediately obvious.. whether it's the product of this dramatic impact or whether it's a captured asteroid. So we'll find that out really quickly."
The team is also hoping there might be an extra bonus coming back to their labs.
"One of the really exciting things is that Phobos is so close to the Mars surface that whenever there's an impact into the Mars surface, little grains might actually become implanted into Phobos itself," said Russell.
"And that means that the sample we get back may actually contain grains of Mars as well. So it can give us really direct information about the composition and history of Mars."
Bringing material from Mars back to Earth has long been an ambition of space scientists.
The Nasa Perseverance rover, which has been exploring Mars since 2021, has been carefully collecting samples on Mars and storing them in canisters.
But a second Nasa/ESA mission, called Mars Sample Return, that would have picked up and returned these canisters, has been effectively cancelled, after its funding was halted by the US Congress.
China is planning its own sampling mission to Mars, set to launch in 2028. It will attempt to return Martian material to Earth in 2031.
We do already have some fragments of the Red Planet here on Earth in the form of Martian meteorites.
These are pieces of Mars that were blasted off the surface by asteroid strikes, and ended up being hurled towards the Earth.
Martian meteorites are extremely rare, but like all space rocks that fall to our planet, they become contaminated as soon as they get here, mixing with the air, dust, soil and water.
Scientists are so desperate to get their gloved hands on a direct sample from Mars and its moons because it would be pristine.
description: A spacecraft is set to launch on an ambitious mission to bring 10g of Martian moon dust back to Earth.
content:
Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon
- Published
A spacecraft has launched from Japan headed for Mars' moon Phobos, where it will attempt to grab some moondust and bring it back to Earth.
If it is successful, this will become the first time a sample has been returned from Mars or its moons to be analysed in laboratories here on Earth.
The spacecraft is scheduled to arrive at Phobos in August 2027.
It is hoped that the Mars Moons Exploration (MMX) mission, which is led by the Japanese Space Agency, will solve the mystery of how Mars's moons formed.
Prof Sara Russell, from the Natural History Museum, who is the MMX mission's deputy for sample analysis, said: "There hasn't yet been a successful mission to go to Phobos and bring a bit back to Earth.
"I think this is an incredibly ambitious and fun mission," she said.
There are only three moons in the inner Solar System: our own Moon, and two around Mars, which are called Phobos and Deimos.
Both of these are tiny - Phobos is about 20km (12 miles) across and Deimos is about 10km (six miles) across. They are also irregularly shaped, looking a bit like space potatoes.
The MMX spacecraft will study Deimos as it arrives in the Mars neighbourhood, and then will focus on Phobos.
It plans to set down a small rover to explore the terrain, though this will be no easy feat.
Sara Russell says no one has ever landed a rover on such a small moon.
"The moon itself doesn't have very much of its own gravity," she explained.
"But it's next to an enormous planet that's got a much higher gravity, and that makes it much harder to get a rover onto the surface."
The rover will scout out a landing site so that the MMX spacecraft itself can later touch down on Phobos.
Once on the surface, it will deploy a robotic arm and two samplers to grab some moon dust.
This material will be packed into a small capsule that will return to Earth in 2031, landing in the Woomera desert of South Australia.
The amount of material that will come back is tiny - just 10g.
"It's a very small [amount] actually," said Dr Chrysa Avdellidou, from Leicester University, who is working with the Japanese mission.
"However we can do several studies even on individual grains… You don't need to have kilos back from a surface in order to do science. So it's worth every gram," she said.
Scientists believe the sample will finally shed light on the puzzle of where Mars's moons came from.
There are two competing ideas.
Either a space rock smashed into Mars early in its history, and Phobos and Deimos were created from the debris.
Or the moons are two wandering asteroids from the outer Solar System, which were grabbed by the Red Planet's gravity.
"When we get the sample back, we'll be able to look in detail at its chemistry and its mineral composition - and the two hypotheses will produce very distinct results," said Sara Russell.
"It should be pretty much immediately obvious.. whether it's the product of this dramatic impact or whether it's a captured asteroid. So we'll find that out really quickly."
The team is also hoping there might be an extra bonus coming back to their labs.
"One of the really exciting things is that Phobos is so close to the Mars surface that whenever there's an impact into the Mars surface, little grains might actually become implanted into Phobos itself," said Russell.
"And that means that the sample we get back may actually contain grains of Mars as well. So it can give us really direct information about the composition and history of Mars."
Bringing material from Mars back to Earth has long been an ambition of space scientists.
The Nasa Perseverance rover, which has been exploring Mars since 2021, has been carefully collecting samples on Mars and storing them in canisters.
But a second Nasa/ESA mission, called Mars Sample Return, that would have picked up and returned these canisters, has been effectively cancelled, after its funding was halted by the US Congress.
China is planning its own sampling mission to Mars, set to launch in 2028. It will attempt to return Martian material to Earth in 2031.
We do already have some fragments of the Red Planet here on Earth in the form of Martian meteorites.
These are pieces of Mars that were blasted off the surface by asteroid strikes, and ended up being hurled towards the Earth.
Martian meteorites are extremely rare, but like all space rocks that fall to our planet, they become contaminated as soon as they get here, mixing with the air, dust, soil and water.
Scientists are so desperate to get their gloved hands on a direct sample from Mars and its moons because it would be pristine.

title: Reform MSP quits party to sit as independent
content_c:
Reform MSP quits party to sit as independent
- Published
MSP Amanda Bland has quit Reform UK Scotland to sit as an independent.
The resignation relegates the party to the third-largest group at Holyrood, with one member fewer than Labour.
A Reform UK source told BBC Scotland News that Bland was "very difficult to work with" and had been called to a meeting on Wednesday to discuss a high turnover of staff in her office.
Bland, who represents Central Scotland and Lothians West, told the BBC that her resignation was not linked to the meeting.
In a statement, she said her "principles and priorities remain unchanged" but gave no further details about her decision.
"I entered politics to champion fairness and common sense, protect women and children, improve public services, support businesses to thrive, and work towards a fairer and more effective criminal justice system," Bland said.
"As a member of the criminal justice committee, I remain committed to scrutinising legislation, holding the justice system to account and supporting practical measures that improve public safety, protect victims and ensure justice is served.
"Holding the Scottish government to account remains a key priority, and I believe I can best pursue these goals as an Independent MSP."
She said she would not be making any further statements or giving interviews about Reform, and that her focus now was on her responsibilities as an independent MSP.
A Reform spokesperson said: "Amanda Bland should reflect on her reasons for choosing to isolate herself from that team of capable individuals.
"It is incumbent on her to resign as a regional MSP for Central Scotland and Lothians West and allow her constituents to be represented by the next Reform candidate on that list."
Under Holyrood's rules, a list MSP would be replaced by their party's next candidate at the last election if they resigned.
Bland, a former primary school teacher and police officer, was among 17 Reform candidates to be returned to the Scottish Parliament in May as the party made its electoral breakthrough north of the border.
The party finished in joint second with Labour, behind the SNP on 58 seats.
Reform's cohort, led by former Conservative minister Malcolm Offord, have repeatedly invoked the condemnation of the chamber - most notably after staging a walkout during an independence debate, and by tabling a motion proposing a burka ban.
Currently, Offord is first to question John Swinney at First Minister's Questions every other week, alternating with Labour. The party is now likely to lose that privilege.
Reform UK says its goal is to disrupt a so-called "cosy consensus" in Scottish politics.
Of the 17 MSPs elected under its banner in May, only one had previous experience at Holyrood.
As party leader, Offord has only had a matter of months to try and turn them into a coherent and cohesive political force.
While Bland's resignation was sudden, some kind of fracture in the group has been widely anticipated.
Reform UK's statement on her departure claims the party has a "united team" at Holyrood - something that will attract much scrutiny and speculation.
Reform 'stunts'
Scottish Labour deputy leader Jackie Baillie said: "No-one will be surprised to see chaos at the heart of Reform."
She said the party had been "utterly useless at holding the SNP to account or getting results for the Scottish people", adding: "It's been a series of stunts, gimmicks, photo calls and precious little else."
The Scottish Conservatives said there were growing questions about Reform's ability to provide effective opposition to the SNP at Holyrood.
A spokesperson said: "With Nigel Farage's Reform being weak and ineffective at Holyrood, the Scottish Conservatives will continue standing up to the SNP and fighting for Scotland's taxpayers."
Scottish Liberal Democrat David Green MSP said that Reform had been hit by "scandal after scandal".
He added: "I'm sure more and more of its MSPs will be taking a long hard look at what they've signed up for."
The Scottish Parliament confirmed Bland's resignation and said its website, external had been updated accordingly.

title: Bikes 'not for jousting,' says Lime after duel video
content_c:
Bikes 'not for jousting,' says Lime after duel video
- Published
E-bike rental company Lime has said its bikes are "not for jousting" after footage of two riders dressed as knights charging at each other in an east London park circulated over the weekend.
Hundreds of people congregated in London Fields, Hackney, to watch artist Jack Carden and actor Camtholomew the First joust, while riding the bright green rentable e-bikes.
The videos on social media showed them dressed as knights in armour, complete with chainmail and lances, attempting to knock each other off the bikes.
A spokesperson for the company said: "While we appreciate the medieval spirit, safety must always come first."
Ahead of the event, Carden said the "free public joust" was "performance art" in a post on social media.
A video on his Instagram account of the event has been watched more than four million times.
Despite their popularity, hospitals have reported an increase in injuries to both e-bike riders and pedestrians.
A spokesperson for Lime said on Monday: "We always love seeing Londoners come together and build a sense of community in unexpected ways.
"While we appreciate the medieval spirit, safety must always come first.
"Lime bikes are designed for getting around the city, not for jousting.
"We discourage anyone from attempting similar events, to help keep riders and those around them safe."

title: Hurricane Trudy menaces Mexico’s Pacific coast and Greece hit by deadly floods
content_c:
In contrast to the quiet Atlantic hurricane season, there has been ongoing activity in the Pacific, with Trudy being the 22nd and latest named system. The category 2 hurricane remained roughly 100 miles (160km) south-west of the coast of Mexico, meaning the worst of the conditions stayed offshore. However, the US National Hurricane Center put coastal parts of the states of Jalisco, Michoacán and Colima under hurricane warnings, with sustained winds of up to 60-90mph forecast on Sunday.
Rainfall totals of 100-150mm were likely for these areas, prompting warnings of flooding and landslides. Warnings also covered the risk of a dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves in areas of onshore winds across the coast of south-western Mexico. By Monday morning, Trudy had weakened and been downgraded to a tropical storm, with coastal warnings being lifted.
In Greece, heavy rain and thunderstorms caused severe flooding and one fatality across Rhodes, Evia and the Sporades islands last week. According to the National Observatory of Athens, a station in Rhodes recorded 202mm between 3.30am and 9.50am (UTC) on 14 October. Regional authorities reported more than 30 rescue and extrication operations in response to flooding, while the Greek coastguard said four passenger vehicles were swept into the sea during the storm. On Skiathos, flood waters swept away two cars.
Five deaths were reported due to severe flooding in Istanbul, Turkey, last week. Heavy rain on 14 and 15 October prompted school closures, flight delays, disruptive flooding and landslides across several provinces. According to the Istanbul metropolitan municipality, 242mm of rain was recorded in Beykoz, a district of Istanbul province. Nearly 600 people were rescued after becoming stranded and at least 2,700 people were forced to evacuate their homes.
The Turkish state meteorological service issued further alerts for heavy rain and thunderstorms over the weekend across dozens of provinces, with at least an additional 40-60mm forecast for parts of the Marmara and western Black Sea regions.

title: No 10: Hegseth ‘wrong’ to say most non-US Nato soldiers didn’t fight in Afghanistan – as it happened
content_c:
No 10 says US defence secretary Pete Hegseth 'wrong' to say most non-US Nato soldiers in Afghanistan didn't fight
Downing Street has delivered a rare public reprimand to a member of Donald Trump’s administration, saying Pete Hegseth, the US defence secretary, was “wrong” to suggest that most non-American Nato soldiers in Afghanistan did not do any fighting.
Hegseth made the comment in a speech at the University of Tennessee, where he recalled serving in Afghanistan himself. He said:
I was a captain in Afghanistan and we would go to the headquarters in Kabul and there would be 50 flags at the headquarters. It was a beautiful thing to see, 50 different countries contributing to the Nato alliance and the Isaf [International Security Assistance Force] mission there.
Except there were maybe five that contributed. It was actually closer to one or two that by the end were actually involved in kinetic operations. In fact the patch Isaf, we joked it meant ‘I Saw Americans Fighting’.
Asked about Hegseth’s comment at the Downing Street lobby briefing, the PM’s spokesperson said Hegseth was “wrong” in what he said about the Nato operation in Afghanistan.
The spokesperson explained:
The facts speak for themselves when it comes to the UK’s and Nato’s contribution to Afghanistan. Thousands of British and Allied families made huge sacrifices to play their significant part in that war and uphold our values, and more than 450 British personnel never returned.
Their sacrifice and that of other Nato forces was made in the service of collective security and in response to an attack on our ally. We are incredibly proud of our armed forces and their service and sacrifice will never be forgotten, and it is wrong to diminish their role.
While the UK government disagrees with much of what Donald Trump and his team say and do, there is normally a reluctance to criticise them in public. However, this does not seem to apply when the reputation of British servicemen and women has been impugned. Keir Starmer tried hard to maintain a good personal relationship with the US president, but when Trump made a similar claim about Nato allies avoiding frontline fighting in Afghanistan, Starmer condemned what he said as “insulting and frankly appalling”.
Scottish Labour has become the second largest party at Holyrood after Amanda Bland, a Reform UK MSP, resigned from the party to sit as an independent. (See 12.21pm.)
Wes Streeting, the defence secretary has said the armed forces need to “live within their means” as he confirmed that some training exercises have been cancelled to save money. (See 2.54pm.)
For a full list of all the stories covered on the blog today, do scroll through the list of key event headlines near the top of the blog.
Miatta Fahnbulleh scrubs post from website criticising Home Office plan to make migrant workers wait much longer for ILR
Miatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, has published an article criticising the home secretary’s proposal to make immigrant workers wait much longer before they can apply for permanent residency in the UK.
In a post on the website that promotes her work as Labour MP for Peckham in south London, she said:
Ultimately, I want to see a system based on control and compassion, with a much stronger focus on integration …
If we continually prolong the time people have to wait for settlement, we can also prolong the process of building cohesion.
We need to raise the level of the debate, challenge divisive political rhetoric and make the case for communities like the one we have in Peckham. That means talking about immigration with care, control and compassion.
According to a story by Nick Gutteridge for the Telegraph, Fahnbulleh’s team say these comments were actually written by an aide as an account of what the MP said at a meeting with consituents last month. They describe it as poorly-phrased summary, and the post has been taken down so that it can be reworded. But they do not seem to be contesting that the public version captures the gist of what she thinks.
The language is contentious because Shabana Mahmood wants to make most migrant workers wait for at least 10 years before they can apply for indefinite leave to remain (ILR) in the UK. Under current rules, ILR is normally available after five years.
Mahmood originally published her plans last year. Fahnbulleh, who came to the UK as a child refugee from Liberia, is not the only cabinet minister with concerns. Andy Burnham has signalled that he is unhappy about Mahmood’s plan to make foreign care workers wait 15 years for ILF (supposedly because their low earnings mean they are more likely to be a burden on the state), and Mahmood has signalled that some sort of climbdown is coming.
The latest edition of the Guardian’s Politics Weekly UK podcast is out. It features Kiran Stacey and Pippa Crerar talking about the Alan Milburn review of youth unemployment.
Welsh first minister invites Burnham to agree 'new partnership for growth' with Wales
Rhun ap Iorwerth, the Welsh first minister, will give a speech later inviting Andy Burnham to agree to a “new partnership'” between Wales and the UK government on growth. The two governments should also avoid “duplicating activity”, he will say.
According to a report for Nation.Cymru, ap Iorwerth will say:
I will invite the prime minister to agree a new partnership for growth between our two governments – a practical agreement about how our two governments work together to unlock Wales’s economic potential …
My message to the prime minister will be a simple one – let us spend less time designing new programmes and duplicating activity. Let us spend more time unlocking opportunity and supporting investment, and more time delivering the growth we both want to see in all parts of our respective nations.
The Green party has reacted with alarm to reports suggesting the Alan Milburn review of Neets will recommend lower sickness benefits for people under the age of 25.
Pointing out that the recent review from Prof Peter Fonagy into the prevalence of mental health conditions, autism and ADHD argued cutting benefits was bad for mental health, the Green party’s co-deputy leader Mothin Ali said:
It seems that when you commission an expert like Prof Fonagy rather than a Blairite former minister, you get a far more coherent analysis of the issues affecting young people and their mental health …
The Green party has a proper jobs guarantee for young people – real jobs, with real training and rights at work. It would be funded by those who can afford to contribute, not by cutting support for those least able to cope.
Streeting rejects call from Tory MP for UK to sell Diego Garcia military base to Trump
During defence questions, Edward Leigh, the Conservative MP and father of the Commons, asked Wes Streeting about the Diego Garcia military base on the Chagos Islands. Given that it was “to all intents and purposes an American military base”, why didn’t the government just sell it to Donald Trump for £6bn, and invest the money in defence?
Streeting said that he didn’t think that was the right solution.
In an earlier answer, Streeting defended the government’s plan to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius as a response the legal doubt over the UK’s claims of ownership. He said:
Having looked at this whole issue with a fresh pair of eyes, I’ve reached the same conclusion as every prime minister since Boris Johnson, including this one, which is the capabilities provided by that base makes it extremely unwise and a risk not worth taking to have legal uncertainty. That is why efforts to negotiate a treaty continue.
Fraser Nelson, the Times columnist who is heavily involved in a project the paper is running investigating the nature of welfare spending, has written an interesting post on his Substack blog about Andy Burnham’s welfare article today. (See 9.34am.) Nelson argues that Burnham saying “benefits will become the backstop, not the starting point” is the key line. He explains:
I read this as an intention to dismantle what Whitehall officials call ‘the pipeline’ – in effect, a Neet factory. Children as young as five are categorised as disabled and a £10k package released to the parents. This ‘disability living allowance’ typically converts to adult Pip at age 16 paying about £9,000 straight to the kid.
Outcomes for such child claimants are poor: the Milburn review disclosed that the DWP holds the power to follow these kids in later life. It does not use this power lest anyone FoIs to find out the scandal (they rejected my request saying it’d cost too much to work out what happened to sickness benefit claimants, even though they could). But [Alan] Milburn used his powers to get them to publish a cohort analysis. This graph is The Pipeline.
And Nelson includes this chart showing what happens to children who have claimed DLA (disability living allowance) for children after the age of 16.
James Cartlidge, the shadow defence secretary, reminded Streeting that, soon after being made defence secretary, he was asked in a TV interview if he would resign if the Treasury did not allocate enough for defence spending. “Absolutely,” Streeting replied. Cartlidge asked if that was still the case.
Streeting said that his answer remained the same. And he said he was confident saying that because “this government is already delivering the biggest sustained increase in defence spending since the end of the cold war”.
Streeting says it is 'irresponsible' and 'inaccurate' for Reform UK to claim Britain cannot defend Falkland Islands
Back in the Commons, Wes Streeting, the defence secretary, is now taking topical questions.
In response to Andrew Rosindell from Reform UK saying the UK’s “ability to protect the Falkland Islands is now in doubt”, Streeting replied:
It is simply irresponsible, not to mention inaccurate, to suggest that the UK is incapable of defending the Falkland Islands. We are perfectly capable of doing that. We had a very visible demonstration only recently. Maybe if Reform had a defence spokesperson, they might have noticed.
Israeli general election highlights flaws with PR, David Blunkett claims
This morning Daisy Cooper cited Andy Burnham’s support for proportional representation as evidence that the Liberal Democrats are “winning the battle of ideas”. (See 11am.)
But only up to a point. There are a couple of reports around this morning that show that, while Burnham may personally favour PR, he is yet to convincingly win the argument for it in the parliamentary Labour party.
In an article for PoliticsHome,Harriet Symonds and Matilda Martin point out that some of Burnham’s most senior ministers prefer first-past-the-post. They say:
PoliticsHome understands that Louise Haigh, deputy PM and Burnham’s close ally, has concerns about shifting to PR.
Other Cabinet members have previously voiced reservations about the idea.
In 2022, Angela Rayner, now secretary of state for housing, communities and local government, said she was a “first-past-the-post girl” who was “yet to be convinced by PR”, telling The News Agents podcast that it could allow extremist parties such as the British National Party (BNP) to win House of Commons seats.
And David Blunkett, the former cabinet minister who has been one of Burnham’s political mentors, has written an article for the i restating his longstanding opposition to PR. He says:
In my view, the argument can’t be that “every vote must count”. Each vote already does count, because in order to have winners and losers, people engage in the process which inevitably means that some voters’ preferences will be cancelled out by a greater number preferring another candidate.
Not everyone can have prizes in a democracy. Some candidates lose, some electors are frustrated and annoyed that their candidate didn’t succeed. Hence, the first set of questions about what it is we think this change is going to improve. The second question is why we would believe that electoral reform would change people’s interest or engagement with politics?
Later this month we will have a demonstration of what is the purest form of proportional representation in the world. Namely, the Israeli general election. If there were ever an example of how tiny minorities representing not only outlandish views, but providing a blockage on progress, compromise and long-term outcomes, it has to be this form of PR.
Streeting tells MPs that US still providing 'vital support' to Ukraine, and it 'does know which side it's on'
Wes Streeting told MPs that the US is still on the side of Ukraine in its war against Russia.
During defence questions, the Lib Dem MP James MacCleary asked about reports that the Ukrainian military were left exposed last week after President Trump reportedly intervened to restrict access to the Starlink internet service for its weapons.
Streeting replied:
It is worth pointing out, after what was unquestionably a challenging week for relations between the United States and Ukraine, that the United States has and does and will continue to provide vital support to Ukraine, whether that’s intelligence sharing or indeed the work we do on procurement with and through the United States, as well as the diplomatic track.
Referring to a meeting he had with Pete Hegseth, his US counterpart, last week, Streeting went on:
This is worth reporting to the house; Pete Hegseth, my US counterpart, was keen to thank the United Kingdom for our leadership of Ukraine.
That would suggest to me the United States does know which side it’s on.
Streeting confirms army has to had cancel some training exercises as cost-cutting measure
Wes Streeting, the defence secretary, is taking questions in the Commons.
When the Reform UK MP Danny Kruger asked him if he agreed it was “absolutely scandalous” that non-essential training had been cancelled by the army, Streeting said that training exercises were taking place for the rest of this year. But he accepted that some future training had been cut.
He told MPs:
When I arrived in the Ministry of Defence, there was an in-year overspend that would have seen us overcommitted by the end of the year.
And, as I did at health, I make absolutely no apology whatsoever for sending a very strong message very early on that, while this government is delivering the biggest sustained increase in defence spending since the end of the cold war, I also expect my department and our armed forces to live within their means.

Often it’s lower paid jobs, and often not as many as they’ve claimed. Continue reading...
author: Andrew Sparrow
content:
No 10 says US defence secretary Pete Hegseth 'wrong' to say most non-US Nato soldiers in Afghanistan didn't fight
Downing Street has delivered a rare public reprimand to a member of Donald Trump’s administration, saying Pete Hegseth, the US defence secretary, was “wrong” to suggest that most non-American Nato soldiers in Afghanistan did not do any fighting.
Hegseth made the comment in a speech at the University of Tennessee, where he recalled serving in Afghanistan himself. He said:
I was a captain in Afghanistan and we would go to the headquarters in Kabul and there would be 50 flags at the headquarters. It was a beautiful thing to see, 50 different countries contributing to the Nato alliance and the Isaf [International Security Assistance Force] mission there.
Except there were maybe five that contributed. It was actually closer to one or two that by the end were actually involved in kinetic operations. In fact the patch Isaf, we joked it meant ‘I Saw Americans Fighting’.
Asked about Hegseth’s comment at the Downing Street lobby briefing, the PM’s spokesperson said Hegseth was “wrong” in what he said about the Nato operation in Afghanistan.
The spokesperson explained:
The facts speak for themselves when it comes to the UK’s and Nato’s contribution to Afghanistan. Thousands of British and Allied families made huge sacrifices to play their significant part in that war and uphold our values, and more than 450 British personnel never returned.
Their sacrifice and that of other Nato forces was made in the service of collective security and in response to an attack on our ally. We are incredibly proud of our armed forces and their service and sacrifice will never be forgotten, and it is wrong to diminish their role.
While the UK government disagrees with much of what Donald Trump and his team say and do, there is normally a reluctance to criticise them in public. However, this does not seem to apply when the reputation of British servicemen and women has been impugned. Keir Starmer tried hard to maintain a good personal relationship with the US president, but when Trump made a similar claim about Nato allies avoiding frontline fighting in Afghanistan, Starmer condemned what he said as “insulting and frankly appalling”.
Scottish Labour has become the second largest party at Holyrood after Amanda Bland, a Reform UK MSP, resigned from the party to sit as an independent. (See 12.21pm.)
Wes Streeting, the defence secretary has said the armed forces need to “live within their means” as he confirmed that some training exercises have been cancelled to save money. (See 2.54pm.)
For a full list of all the stories covered on the blog today, do scroll through the list of key event headlines near the top of the blog.
Miatta Fahnbulleh scrubs post from website criticising Home Office plan to make migrant workers wait much longer for ILR
Miatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, has published an article criticising the home secretary’s proposal to make immigrant workers wait much longer before they can apply for permanent residency in the UK.
In a post on the website that promotes her work as Labour MP for Peckham in south London, she said:
Ultimately, I want to see a system based on control and compassion, with a much stronger focus on integration …
If we continually prolong the time people have to wait for settlement, we can also prolong the process of building cohesion.
We need to raise the level of the debate, challenge divisive political rhetoric and make the case for communities like the one we have in Peckham. That means talking about immigration with care, control and compassion.
According to a story by Nick Gutteridge for the Telegraph, Fahnbulleh’s team say these comments were actually written by an aide as an account of what the MP said at a meeting with consituents last month. They describe it as poorly-phrased summary, and the post has been taken down so that it can be reworded. But they do not seem to be contesting that the public version captures the gist of what she thinks.
The language is contentious because Shabana Mahmood wants to make most migrant workers wait for at least 10 years before they can apply for indefinite leave to remain (ILR) in the UK. Under current rules, ILR is normally available after five years.
Mahmood originally published her plans last year. Fahnbulleh, who came to the UK as a child refugee from Liberia, is not the only cabinet minister with concerns. Andy Burnham has signalled that he is unhappy about Mahmood’s plan to make foreign care workers wait 15 years for ILF (supposedly because their low earnings mean they are more likely to be a burden on the state), and Mahmood has signalled that some sort of climbdown is coming.
The latest edition of the Guardian’s Politics Weekly UK podcast is out. It features Kiran Stacey and Pippa Crerar talking about the Alan Milburn review of youth unemployment.
Welsh first minister invites Burnham to agree 'new partnership for growth' with Wales
Rhun ap Iorwerth, the Welsh first minister, will give a speech later inviting Andy Burnham to agree to a “new partnership'” between Wales and the UK government on growth. The two governments should also avoid “duplicating activity”, he will say.
According to a report for Nation.Cymru, ap Iorwerth will say:
I will invite the prime minister to agree a new partnership for growth between our two governments – a practical agreement about how our two governments work together to unlock Wales’s economic potential …
My message to the prime minister will be a simple one – let us spend less time designing new programmes and duplicating activity. Let us spend more time unlocking opportunity and supporting investment, and more time delivering the growth we both want to see in all parts of our respective nations.
The Green party has reacted with alarm to reports suggesting the Alan Milburn review of Neets will recommend lower sickness benefits for people under the age of 25.
Pointing out that the recent review from Prof Peter Fonagy into the prevalence of mental health conditions, autism and ADHD argued cutting benefits was bad for mental health, the Green party’s co-deputy leader Mothin Ali said:
It seems that when you commission an expert like Prof Fonagy rather than a Blairite former minister, you get a far more coherent analysis of the issues affecting young people and their mental health …
The Green party has a proper jobs guarantee for young people – real jobs, with real training and rights at work. It would be funded by those who can afford to contribute, not by cutting support for those least able to cope.
Streeting rejects call from Tory MP for UK to sell Diego Garcia military base to Trump
During defence questions, Edward Leigh, the Conservative MP and father of the Commons, asked Wes Streeting about the Diego Garcia military base on the Chagos Islands. Given that it was “to all intents and purposes an American military base”, why didn’t the government just sell it to Donald Trump for £6bn, and invest the money in defence?
Streeting said that he didn’t think that was the right solution.
In an earlier answer, Streeting defended the government’s plan to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius as a response the legal doubt over the UK’s claims of ownership. He said:
Having looked at this whole issue with a fresh pair of eyes, I’ve reached the same conclusion as every prime minister since Boris Johnson, including this one, which is the capabilities provided by that base makes it extremely unwise and a risk not worth taking to have legal uncertainty. That is why efforts to negotiate a treaty continue.
Fraser Nelson, the Times columnist who is heavily involved in a project the paper is running investigating the nature of welfare spending, has written an interesting post on his Substack blog about Andy Burnham’s welfare article today. (See 9.34am.) Nelson argues that Burnham saying “benefits will become the backstop, not the starting point” is the key line. He explains:
I read this as an intention to dismantle what Whitehall officials call ‘the pipeline’ – in effect, a Neet factory. Children as young as five are categorised as disabled and a £10k package released to the parents. This ‘disability living allowance’ typically converts to adult Pip at age 16 paying about £9,000 straight to the kid.
Outcomes for such child claimants are poor: the Milburn review disclosed that the DWP holds the power to follow these kids in later life. It does not use this power lest anyone FoIs to find out the scandal (they rejected my request saying it’d cost too much to work out what happened to sickness benefit claimants, even though they could). But [Alan] Milburn used his powers to get them to publish a cohort analysis. This graph is The Pipeline.
And Nelson includes this chart showing what happens to children who have claimed DLA (disability living allowance) for children after the age of 16.
James Cartlidge, the shadow defence secretary, reminded Streeting that, soon after being made defence secretary, he was asked in a TV interview if he would resign if the Treasury did not allocate enough for defence spending. “Absolutely,” Streeting replied. Cartlidge asked if that was still the case.
Streeting said that his answer remained the same. And he said he was confident saying that because “this government is already delivering the biggest sustained increase in defence spending since the end of the cold war”.
Streeting says it is 'irresponsible' and 'inaccurate' for Reform UK to claim Britain cannot defend Falkland Islands
Back in the Commons, Wes Streeting, the defence secretary, is now taking topical questions.
In response to Andrew Rosindell from Reform UK saying the UK’s “ability to protect the Falkland Islands is now in doubt”, Streeting replied:
It is simply irresponsible, not to mention inaccurate, to suggest that the UK is incapable of defending the Falkland Islands. We are perfectly capable of doing that. We had a very visible demonstration only recently. Maybe if Reform had a defence spokesperson, they might have noticed.
Israeli general election highlights flaws with PR, David Blunkett claims
This morning Daisy Cooper cited Andy Burnham’s support for proportional representation as evidence that the Liberal Democrats are “winning the battle of ideas”. (See 11am.)
But only up to a point. There are a couple of reports around this morning that show that, while Burnham may personally favour PR, he is yet to convincingly win the argument for it in the parliamentary Labour party.
In an article for PoliticsHome,Harriet Symonds and Matilda Martin point out that some of Burnham’s most senior ministers prefer first-past-the-post. They say:
PoliticsHome understands that Louise Haigh, deputy PM and Burnham’s close ally, has concerns about shifting to PR.
Other Cabinet members have previously voiced reservations about the idea.
In 2022, Angela Rayner, now secretary of state for housing, communities and local government, said she was a “first-past-the-post girl” who was “yet to be convinced by PR”, telling The News Agents podcast that it could allow extremist parties such as the British National Party (BNP) to win House of Commons seats.
And David Blunkett, the former cabinet minister who has been one of Burnham’s political mentors, has written an article for the i restating his longstanding opposition to PR. He says:
In my view, the argument can’t be that “every vote must count”. Each vote already does count, because in order to have winners and losers, people engage in the process which inevitably means that some voters’ preferences will be cancelled out by a greater number preferring another candidate.
Not everyone can have prizes in a democracy. Some candidates lose, some electors are frustrated and annoyed that their candidate didn’t succeed. Hence, the first set of questions about what it is we think this change is going to improve. The second question is why we would believe that electoral reform would change people’s interest or engagement with politics?
Later this month we will have a demonstration of what is the purest form of proportional representation in the world. Namely, the Israeli general election. If there were ever an example of how tiny minorities representing not only outlandish views, but providing a blockage on progress, compromise and long-term outcomes, it has to be this form of PR.
Streeting tells MPs that US still providing 'vital support' to Ukraine, and it 'does know which side it's on'
Wes Streeting told MPs that the US is still on the side of Ukraine in its war against Russia.
During defence questions, the Lib Dem MP James MacCleary asked about reports that the Ukrainian military were left exposed last week after President Trump reportedly intervened to restrict access to the Starlink internet service for its weapons.
Streeting replied:
It is worth pointing out, after what was unquestionably a challenging week for relations between the United States and Ukraine, that the United States has and does and will continue to provide vital support to Ukraine, whether that’s intelligence sharing or indeed the work we do on procurement with and through the United States, as well as the diplomatic track.
Referring to a meeting he had with Pete Hegseth, his US counterpart, last week, Streeting went on:
This is worth reporting to the house; Pete Hegseth, my US counterpart, was keen to thank the United Kingdom for our leadership of Ukraine.
That would suggest to me the United States does know which side it’s on.
Streeting confirms army has to had cancel some training exercises as cost-cutting measure
Wes Streeting, the defence secretary, is taking questions in the Commons.
When the Reform UK MP Danny Kruger asked him if he agreed it was “absolutely scandalous” that non-essential training had been cancelled by the army, Streeting said that training exercises were taking place for the rest of this year. But he accepted that some future training had been cut.
He told MPs:
When I arrived in the Ministry of Defence, there was an in-year overspend that would have seen us overcommitted by the end of the year.
And, as I did at health, I make absolutely no apology whatsoever for sending a very strong message very early on that, while this government is delivering the biggest sustained increase in defence spending since the end of the cold war, I also expect my department and our armed forces to live within their means.

title: Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
content_c:
Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
October 19, 2026
Bulgaria on Monday issued European arrest warrants against two 19-year-old German nationals, saying it suspected their involvement in the sabotage of a series of Starlink antennas near the capital Sofia.
"The evidence gathered makes it possible to conclude that there are reasonable grounds to suspect the involvement of the two defendants," the court in Sofia rules, granting a request from prosecutors.
Ukraine's military uses Starlink's military-grade satellite internet service Starshield for battlefield communications amid Russia's invasion.
Bulgaria does not directly border Ukraine, but it is on the Black Sea, one of the flashpoints of the conflict. A similar case in Poland, which does directly border Ukraine, led to a total of four arrests last week, also in Germany.
What do we know about the incident in Bulgaria?
The two teenage suspects are accused of deliberately setting fire to the antennas on the evening of October 9.
Of 18 in a mountainous region south of Sofia, three were destroyed entirely, two were partially burned and three more were damaged, according to prosecutors.
Prosecutors say the suspects entered from Serbia in a car with German license plates, claiming to be tourists, staying just a few hours around the time of the alleged crime.
Plamen Tonchev, the head of Bulgaria's domestic intelligence agency DANS, said he was working on the assumption that it was deliberate sabotage and said other such acts could not be ruled out in future.
What is the potential tie-in to a Polish sabotage case?
News of the arrests follow just a week after a total of four people were arrested in Germany, accused of sabotaging a Starlink satellite communications station in central Poland in late September.
German police detained three resident men and a woman, two of them Turkish nationals, early last week.
Polish officials said they believed that Russia was behind the sabotage attempt, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk calling it an act of "hybrid warfare."
The domestic intelligence agency also claimed that Russia had cooperated with organized crime elements in Germany on the alleged operation.
Meanwhile, in the Baltic, Lithuania's prime minister on Sunday said that Russia was likely behind an attempted arson attack on a company hosting communication hardware for Starlink satellites.
Edited by: Wesley Dockery

title: Arzttermine: Kassenärzte warnen vor längeren Wartezeiten durch Reform
content_c:
Warnung der Kassenärzte Patienten werden noch länger auf Termine warten müssen
Wer gesetzlich krankenversichert ist, muss schon jetzt oft lange auf einen Arzttermin warten . Künftig drohen noch längere Wartezeiten, warnen die Kassenärzte: Der Vorsitzende der Kassenärztlichen Bundesvereinigung (KBV), Andreas Gassen, sagte der »Bild«-Zeitung, durch die Kürzung der Mittel für die ambulante Versorgung habe die Bundesregierung gerade mehr als 50 Millionen Termine in der ambulanten Versorgung gestrichen.
»Dass Arztpraxen künftig eine fixe Zahl an freien Terminen melden müssen, wird nicht dazu führen, dass Patienten schneller an Termine kommen. Im Gegenteil: Wird ein festes Kontingent zu meldender Termine festgelegt und diese damit in den Praxen blockiert, stehen diese nicht mehr für die Patienten in diesen Praxen zur Verfügung«, sagte KBV-Chef Gassen. »Die Terminnot wird sich also weiter verschärfen.«
KBV-Chef Gassen: »Die Terminnot wird sich weiter verschärfen«
Foto:
Britta Pedersen / dpa
Gassen betonte, die KBV habe genau darauf immer wieder hingewiesen. »Nur wenn mehr Geld für die ambulante Versorgung zur Verfügung steht, wird es mehr Termine geben können. Das sind vergleichsweise einfach zu verstehende wirtschaftliche Abhängigkeiten.«
Die KBV hatte eine erweiterte »Terminmeldepflicht« im Zuge der kürzlich beschlossenen Reform der Notfallversorgung kritisiert. Bisher waren Vertragsärzte verpflichtet, der Terminservicestelle freie Termine zu melden. Sie konnten den Umfang demnach selbst bestimmen. Künftig soll es feste Kontingente für Termine geben, die sie melden müssen.
Nach der jüngst vom Bundestag beschlossenen Reform sind die Vertragsärzte verpflichtet, der Terminservicestelle »Termine in dem von den Kassenärztlichen Vereinigung im Einvernehmen mit den Landesverbänden der Kranken- und Ersatzkassen festzulegenden Umfang zu melden«. Erst streiche die Politik die extrabudgetäre Vergütung für zusätzliche Termine, dann verschärfe sie die Meldepflicht, hatte KBV-Chef Gassen zuletzt kritisiert.
Fast nirgendwo geht es so ungerecht zu wie in deutschen Arztpraxen: Kassenpatienten warten ewig, Privatkunden werden bevorzugt. Wie das Zwei-Klassen-System das Grundvertrauen der Deutschen in einen fairen Staat beschädigt, erfahren Sie in dieser SPIEGEL-Titelstory.
description: Gesetzlich Krankenversicherte müssen vom kommenden Jahr an noch länger warten, bis sie einen Termin bekommen, warnt Kassenärzte-Chef Gassen. Als Grund nennt er die Reform der Bundesregierung.

title: Verbaler Schlagabtausch: Neue Spannungen zwischen Trump und Selenskyj
content_c:
Verbaler Schlagabtausch Neue Spannungen zwischen Trump und Selenskyj
"Wir haben der Ukraine viel gegeben - sie hat uns nichts gegeben": US-Präsident Trump verschärft den Ton gegen Selenskyj. Der ukrainische Präsident wiederum wirft den USA vor, Waffenlieferungen zurückzuhalten.
US-Präsident Donald Trump hat der Ukraine fehlende Gegenleistungen für die Unterstützung der USA vorgeworfen. "Wir haben der Ukraine viel gegeben - sie hat uns nichts gegeben. Vergessen Sie das nicht", sagte er in Washington.
Nach Ansicht von Trump sollte anstelle des ukrainischen Staatsoberhaupts Wolodymyr Selenskyj jemand anderes die Friedensverhandlungen mit Russland führen. "Vielleicht ist es für Selenskyj an der Zeit, jemand anderen verhandeln zu lassen", sagt Trump vor Journalisten.
Er hatte vor Kurzem eine Ablösung des ukrainischen Staatschefs gefordert. Russland verhalte sich mit Blick auf die Ukraine "in Ordnung" und mache "nicht viel", fügte Trump hinzu. Er zeigte sich zudem offen für einen Dreiergipfel mit Kremlchef Putin und Chinas Staatschef Xi am Rande des Treffens der Apec-Staaten in China im November.
Selenskyj beklagt verzögerte Lieferung von Abwehrraketen
Derweil beklagte Selenskyj, dass Washington Waffenlieferungen zurückhalte. Verzögerungen bei Waffenlieferungen und Einschränkungen beim Austausch von Geheimdienstinformationen seien "unter Freunden schwer zu erklären", sagte er bei einem Treffen mit einer US-Kongressdelegation.
Selenskyj zufolge genehmige Verteidigungsminister Pete Hegseth die Lieferung von "Patriot"- und weiteren Luftabwehr-Raketen nicht, obwohl NATO-Staaten diese bereits bezahlt hätten. "All das deutet darauf hin, dass eine politische Entscheidung getroffen wurde, die Unterstützung für uns zurückzufahren", sagte Selenskyj.
Ein hochrangiger Beamter aus dem Verteidigungsministerium trat den Darstellungen entgegen. Bei dem Programm, mit dem NATO-Staaten US-Waffen für die Ukraine kaufen, habe es keine Änderungen gegeben, sagte er der Nachrichtenagentur dpa. Dasselbe gelte für den Austausch von Geheimdienstinformationen.

title: Roma gegen Hitler: Tschechien würdigt Widerstandskämpfer
content_c:
Roma gegen Hitler: Tschechien würdigt Widerstandskämpfer
19. Oktober 2026
Für mehr als eine halbe Million Roma in Tschechien und der Slowakei war der 15. Oktober 2026 ein bedeutender Tag. An diesem Tag wurde im Prager "Museum der nationalen Wiedergeburt der Roma" eine Ausstellung über ein weitgehend vergessenes Kapitel tschechoslowakischer Geschichte eröffnet - eine Ausstellung über tschechische und slowakische Roma-Widerstandskämpfer während der nationalsozialistischen deutschen Besatzung und Zerschlagung der Tschechoslowakei von 1938 bis 1945.
Bislang tauchten die tschechischen und slowakischen Roma in der Geschichte des Zweiten Weltkriegs fast ausschließlich als Opfer des Holocausts an Roma und Sinti auf. Im sogenannten Protektorat Böhmen und Mähren ermordeten die deutschen Nationalsozialisten während des Zweiten Weltkriegs rund neunzig Prozent der tschechischen Roma.
Weniger bekannt ist, dass eine große Zahl tschechischer und slowakischer Roma als Partisanen in Widerstandsgruppen und Soldaten der tschechoslowakischen Untergrundarmee (Verteidigung der Nation, ON) gegen die deutschen Besatzer kämpften. Dokumentiert sind die Beispiele von mehr als 1400 Personen. Diesem Kapitel des bewaffneten Widerstands der Roma gegen die Nazis ist die Ausstellung im Museum der nationalen Wiedergeburt der Roma gewidmet.
Sie markiert einen Wendepunkt der Sichtweise auf die Roma während des Zweiten Weltkriegs - so hofft es jedenfalls der Museumsdirektor Emil Scuka, Jurist, ehemaliger Staatsanwalt und einer der bekanntesten tschechischen Roma-Aktivisten. "Wir waren nicht nur Opfer, wir waren auch Helden", sagte Scuka bei der Eröffnung der Ausstellung. "Dass wir Roma gegen den Nationalsozialismus gekämpft haben, wissen viele Menschen nicht, nicht einmal unter den Roma selbst."
Auch Roma haben Helden
Der Museumsdirektor Emil Scuka sprach vor mehreren hundert Teilnehmern der Vernissage, bei denen es sich überwiegend um Roma aus Tschechien und der Slowakei handelte. Die Ausstellung zu konzipieren und zu eröffnen, so Scuka, "war etwas, was meine Generation diesen Roma-Helden schuldig war, und diese Schuld begleichen wir heute". Der Museumsdirektor forderte die Anwesenden auf: "Bringen Sie Ihre Kinder und Enkelkinder hierher, damit sie sich ein Bild machen und erkennen, dass auch die Roma ihre Helden haben!"
Scuka wies auch darauf hin, dass dieses Thema in der tschechischen und slowakischen Geschichtsschreibung jahrzehntelang völlig am Rande des Interesses gestanden habe und Roma daher selbst beschlossen hätten, die Schicksale ihrer Kriegshelden eigenständig zu dokumentieren.
Die Ausstellung zeigt die detaillierte Lebensgeschichten von 100 der bedeutendsten Roma-Partisanen und Roma-Soldaten der tschechischen Untergrundarmee und der Widerstandgruppen, die gegen den Nationalsozialismus kämpften. "Wir haben in den Archiven über 1.400 Roma-Kämpfer gefunden. Davon haben wir für diese Ausstellung die hundert interessantesten Schicksale ausgewählt", sagte der Kurator der Ausstellung, Radoslav Scuka, bei der Eröffnung.
Keine Forschung zum Thema
Zu diesen Persönlichkeiten gehört beispielsweise Anton Facuna, ein Unteroffizier des amerikanischen Geheimdienstes OSS, der im Oktober 1944 mit einer geheimen Mission per Flugzeug in die Slowakei gebracht wurde - die von 1939 bis 1945 ein Marionettenstaat Hitlers war.
Ein weiterer ist Josef Serinek, bekannt unter dem Spitznamen "Der schwarze Partisan aus der Vysocina", dem die Flucht aus dem nationalsozialistischen Konzentrationslager für Roma in Lety gelang und der anschließend in der Böhmisch-Mährischen Hochebene die große Partisaneneinheit "Capajev-Cerny" gründete und befehligte. Im Jahr 2022 verlieh ihm der tschechische Präsident Milos Zeman posthum die Medaille für Heldentum. Am Ende seines Lebens teilte Serinek seine Erinnerungen mit dem Historiker Jan Tesar, der daraufhin das dreiteilige Buch "Ceská cikanska rapsodie" (Tschechische Zigeuner-Rhapsodie) verfasste.
Mit Ausnahme von Tesars Buch wurde die Geschichte des Roma-Widerstands gegen den Nationalsozialismus von tschechischen und slowakischen Historikern bis heute nicht erforscht. "Mir ist keine wissenschaftliche historische Arbeit bekannt, die sich mit dem Widerstand der Roma gegen den Nationalsozialismus befasst", sagte Prokop Tomek, Historiker am Militärhistorischen Institut in Prag, der DW.
"Die Schätzung von 1400 Roma, die sich in den Reihen der Widerstandskämpfer und der ausländischen Armee am Kampf gegen den Nationalsozialismus beteiligt haben, erscheint mir nicht übertrieben und entspricht dem Anteil der Roma-Bevölkerung in der Tschechoslowakei", kommentiert Tomek die Schätzungen der Organisatoren der Ausstellung im Prager Roma-Museum. "Die Ausstellung über den Widerstand der Roma gegen den Nationalsozialismus während des Krieges ist zweifellos bahnbrechend", fügt Tomek hinzu.
Angst, sich als Roma zu bekennen
Viele Roma in Tschechien und der Slowakei bekennen sich bis heute öffentlich nicht zu ihrer ethnischen Zugehörigkeit. Dies liegt auch an den über Generationen weitergegebenen Erfahrungen mit dem Holocaust während der nationalsozialistischen Zeit. Tschechische Historiker und Politiker streiten bis heute darüber, inwieweit die tschechischen Behörden des Protektorats an der Vernichtung der tschechischen Roma beteiligt waren. Soviel ist jedoch klar: Die in der Tschechoslowakei seit 1927 gesetzlich verankerte polizeiliche Erfassung aller Roma erleichterte den deutschen Nationalsozialisten die Vernichtung der Volksgruppe.
Nach Schätzungen der tschechischen Regierung leben im Land heute rund 250.000 Roma. Bei der Volkszählung im Jahr 2021 gaben jedoch nur 21.000 Personen diese ethnische Zugehörigkeit an, also weniger als ein Zehntel der tatsächlichen Zahl. Von allen ethnischen Gruppen im zehn Millionen Einwohner zählenden Tschechien gehören die Roma zwar zu den drei zahlenmäßig stärksten ethnischen Minderheiten, sind jedoch sozial am schlechtesten gestellt, verfügen nur über sehr wenige politische Vertretungen und sind daher in der tschechischen Politik nur wenig präsent.
Zwei wichtige Gremien für Roma in Tschechien sind der Regierungsrat für Roma sowie die Regierungsbeauftragte für Roma-Angelegenheiten. Im Juni 2026 traten die Beauftragte Lucie Fukova und sechs Roma-Vertreter des 15-köpfigen Regierungsrats zurück, weil die Kompetenzen für Roma-Angelegenheiten von der gesamten Regierungsebene auf eine niedere Ebene in das Arbeitsministerium verlagert worden waren. Daran hatte unter anderem der tschechische Ombudsmann Kritik geübt. Auch viele Roma-Aktivisten sehen darin eine Schwächung der Roma-Agenda auf Regierungsebene.
Dass die rechtsliberal-populistische Regierung des Premiers Andrej Babis Roma-Angelegenheiten keine besondere Aufmerksamkeit widmet, war auch am Freitag bei der Ausstellungseröffnung zu erkennen: Einen Vertreter oder eine Vertreterin hatte die Regierung nicht entsandt.

title: Яке церковне свято в Україні 21 жовтня
content_c:
Яке церковне свято в Україні 21 жовтня
Що за церковне свято святкують в Україні за новим і старим календарем і кому моляться віряни — читайте в матеріалі ТСН.ua.
21 жовтня (3 листопада), в православному календарі день пам’яті преподобного Іларіона Великого. Іларіон народився близько 291 року в Палестині, неподалік міста Газа, у язичницькій родині. Ще в юному віці він вирушив до Александрії, де здобував освіту.
Саме там Іларіон познайомився з християнською вірою та прийняв хрещення. Поступово він вирішив повністю присвятити себе Богові та відмовитися від звичайного мирського життя.
Важливою подією в житті Іларіона стала зустріч із преподобним Антонієм Великим — одним із найвідоміших засновників християнського чернецтва.
Іларіон деякий час перебував поруч зі святим Антонієм, навчаючись у нього духовної мудрості та правил аскетичного життя. Після цього він повернувся до Палестини, бажаючи продовжити подвижницький шлях уже на батьківщині.
Після смерті батьків Іларіон роздав майно нужденним і вирушив у пустелю. Там він оселився в усамітненому місці неподалік Майуми.
Життя преподобного Іларіона було надзвичайно суворим. Він багато молився, постив, працював руками та намагався якомога менше спілкуватися з людьми.
За переказами, спочатку Іларіон жив у невеликій хатині, харчуючись дуже скромно. Він прагнув перемогти власні пристрасті та повністю зосередитися на духовному житті.
Згодом навколо подвижника почали збиратися люди, які хотіли навчитися в нього християнського життя. Так поступово виникла одна з перших чернечих громад Палестини.
Останні роки преподобний Іларіон провів на острові Кіпр. Там він оселився у віддаленому місці та продовжував подвиг молитви.
За церковним переказом, перед смертю він залишив своїм учням духовні настанови та заповів поховати його скромно.
Преподобний Іларіон Великий помер близько 371 року.
Церковне свято в Україні 21 жовтня за старим календарем
За старим календарем 21 жовтня в Україні вшановували пам’ять преподобної Пелагеї Антіохійської. Пелагея була відома своєю красою та заможністю. Вона жила у світі, сповненому розваг і спокус, однак одного разу почула проповідь єпископа Нонна, який говорив про гріх, покаяння та спасіння душі. Ці слова справили на неї надзвичайно сильне враження. Свята усвідомила помилковість свого попереднього життя і вирішила докорінно його змінити. Пелагея прийняла християнство та щиро розкаялася у своїх гріхах.
Прикмети 21 жовтня
- Якщо 21 жовтня тепло і сонячно — осінь ще довго не відступатиме.
- Сильний вітер цього дня віщує холодну та вітряну погоду найближчими днями.
- Якщо вранці туман — день буде теплим, а погода може незабаром змінитися.
Що не можна робити 21 жовтня
Вважалося, що дорога може виявитися неспокійною або принести неприємні несподіванки, тому подорожі краще було відкласти.
Що можна робити 21 жовтня
У народі його називають Іларіоновим днем і вважають своєрідною межею між осінню та зимою: тепла пора вже добігає кінця, однак справжні зимові холоди ще не настали.

У народі його називають Іларіоновим днем і вважають своєрідною межею між осінню та зимою: тепла пора вже добігає кінця, однак справжні зимові холоди ще не настали.

title: Удар по производственно-складскому зданию в Киевской области: есть погибшие и пострадавшие
content_c:
В ночь на 20 октября российские войска атаковали производственно-складское здание в одной из громад Обуховского района Киевской области. В результате удара три человека погибли, ещё шестеро получили ранения, сообщает Государственная служба по чрезвычайным ситуациям (ГСЧС) в своём Telegram-канале. В ведомстве также опубликовали фото и видео последствий вражеской атаки.
Отмечается, что спасатели потушили пожар и продолжают разбирать завалы. На месте также работали психологи ГСЧС.
Напомним, утром 19 октября российские войска атаковали Ирпень в пригороде Киева баллистическими ракетами. В результате удара в городе были повреждены жилые дома и загорелось предприятие. Тогда пострадали шесть человек, среди них — трое детей.
Всего в Бучанском районе в результате ночной атаки были повреждены 11 частных домов, шесть автомобилей, производственные и складские помещения, а также учебное заведение. В многоквартирных домах также выбиты окна. В Вышгородском районе повреждены частный дом, пять автомобилей и объект инфраструктуры.
Ранее, а именно 15 октября, российские реактивные дроны-камикадзе атаковали Бучанский и Вышгородский районы Киевской области. В селе Петрушки Бучанского района в результате удара загорелись частный дом и две хозяйственные постройки, а 66-летняя местная жительница получила осколочные ранения лица и была госпитализирована.
