title: French authorities announce partial curfews as PM blames ‘ultra-left’ for exploiting protests – as it happened
content_c:
Partial curfews have been issued for a number of French cities, including parts of Paris, after the government admitted police had “lost control” during violent weekend protests around the country. An overnight curfew will come into effect from 11pm until 6am local time, for Place de la Republique and the streets around Les Halles in Paris. Authorities earlier issued the country’s first curfew the northern city of Lille and surrounding cities of Douai, Wattignies and Denain. Curfews were also announced in the southern cities of Nice (specifically for minors) and central Lyon, while Marseille, earlier announced independently that it had banned all gatherings and demonstrations on Monday.
It came after France’s PM, Sébastien Lecornu, said after an emergency cabinet meeting that he was “fully resolved to restore public order” and had called for “local and partial” curfews if needed. There was “no question” of imposing a full curfew on entire cities, he said. Lecornu told reporters that if declaring a state of emergency was deemed necessary “we could do so”, but added that at this stage partial curfews seemed “more appropriate”.
France’s interior minister conceded that police had “lost control” in some cities during Saturday’s protests and the president, Emmanuel Macron, demanded a full security review and “new operational methods” to end the rioting. Laurent Nuñez said there had been a “lack of anticipation” in preparations for the protests and acknowledged that police numbers had sometimes been inadequate to deal with rioters and looters on the fringes of the demonstrations. Nuñez said intelligence had suggested there would be 200,000 demonstrators around the country. In the event, there were more than half a million and peaceful protests were hijacked, morphing into one of France’s most violent days of unrest in recent years. Almost 2,400 arrests have been made.
Nuñez said he had offered his resignation to Macron because he felt “responsible for everything that happened”, but the president had refused it, demanding instead that Nuñez “take all necessary steps to ensure transparency over planning and intelligence failures”. “You couldn’t look shopkeepers in the eye after hundreds of shops had been looted and say we hadn’t lost control,” the minister told French radio, but added that the responsibility of “rioters, looters and ultra-left militants” should not be glossed over.
The original protests, led by students, teachers, parents, unions and workers, focused on the high cost of living, an issue that also prompted demonstrations in several other European countries including Italy, Belgium and Albania over the weekend.
Trump refuses to drop false immigration claim when asked about France protests
Shrai Popat
Ahead of leaving for a campaign rally in Wichita, Kansas, Donald Trumpagain claimed – without evidence – that the riots throughout France are due to mass migration.
“I told Emmanuel [Macron], you should close up your borders,” the US president said. “I’ve known him for probably eight or nine years. I told him as soon as I met him, I said, ‘you’re making a big mistake’. We closed our borders. He didn’t.”
Analysis: Ferocious criticism from all sides underlines Macron’s isolation
Jon Henley
in Paris
The near-universal chorus of condemnation that greeted Emmanuel Macron’s address to the nation on Sunday, after one of the most violent days of rioting and looting in France’s recent history, was a stark reflection of just how weakened he now is.
A month-long protest by high school pupils over crumbling and crowded classrooms converged with broader frustrations over soaring living costs, rapidly widening inequality and falling public spending, bringing together students, teachers, trade unionists and a resurrected gilets jaunes movement.
Those largely peaceful protests were swiftly hijacked by masked groups who torched vehicles, ransacked businesses and severely damaged public infrastructure, including setting fire to Limoges’ city hall and invading that of Marseille.
Macron acknowledged the “deep anxiety” of young people but offered no concrete policy initiatives, no cabinet reshuffle and no new public spending, merely telling his prime minister to organise consultations and asking opposition politicians to take a stand.
The response, across the political spectrum, was damning. The Greens’ leader, Marine Tondelier, said that rather than “even beginning to make any kind of mea culpa”, Macron was “summoning us to the PM’s office like pupils to the blackboard”.
On the far right, the National Rally’s Jordan Bardella called the speech “lamentable” and said Macron had “nothing left to say” to the French. The party’s figurehead, Marine Le Pen, said the country was “caught in a vice between violence and impotence”.
The centre-right’s Bruno Retailleau said Macron was “totally overwhelmed”, while on the radical left, Jean-Luc Mélenchon accused the president of relying on “inaction and police brutality” in doomed hopes that the protests would simply fizzle out.
Perhaps most damagingly, even Macron’s former prime minister Édouard Philippe said he would have preferred “decisions and initiatives that might lead to a return to order and the restoration of state authority … Our country needs to be governed.”
Criticism is to be expected from rivals positioning themselves six months before a presidential election to choose Macron’s successor. But its sheer ferocity underlines his isolation, the disdain in which he is held, and the anger he inspires.
It’s a structural trap that he has largely set for himself. Macron came to power in 2017 as a “Jupiterian” president – a deliberate strategy aimed at elevating the head of state above daily politics, projecting distant authority and technocratic brilliance.
But over nine years in the Élysée, that high-handed style – partly born, his critics say, of Macron’s complete lack of basic political experience as an elected official in a town hall or as a constituency MP – has morphed into perceived arrogance and detachment.
It has been compounded by catastrophic strategic errors, and France’s spiralling economic problems. Macron lost a functional parliamentary majority by refusing to meaningfully campaign between the presidential and legislative elections of 2022.
Two years later he dissolved the national assembly. That gamble backfired spectacularly, with voters returning an even more deadlocked parliament split between a divided left, a much-diminished centrist bloc and Le Pen’s far right.
Without a working majority, the government repeatedly resorted to controversial constitutional manoeuvres to force through laws without a parliamentary vote, laying it – and Macron – open to further accusations of democratic illegitimacy.
Compounding that institutional deadlock is a looming fiscal crisis. In decades gone by, French presidents facing mass protests on the streets could in effect buy a degree of social tranquility with targeted spending packages or public sector concessions.
But France’s national debt, at 119% of GDP, is at its highest level since 1946. Its budget deficit, at 5.1%, is also among the highest in the EU. There is just no money in the bank to ease the cost of living squeeze that brought 550,000 people on to the streets on Saturday.
The markets are worried: France’s borrowing costs are higher than Greece’s. And with few fiscal options, the government’s clearest response – in time-honoured French tradition – has been teargas and baton charges, sometimes against schoolchildren, further aggravating tensions.
The consequences for the presidential election could be profound. The centrist coalition built around Macron’s brand has all but collapsed. If the protests and violence persist, the main beneficiary will be the law-and-order champions of the far right.
US advises Americans to avoid protest areas in France
The US state department has issued an alert warning Americans to avoid demonstration areas in major French cities after days of violent protests that have rocked the country.
The alert issued by the US embassy in Paris noted violent demonstrations on 17 October and the new curfews planned in cities including Lille and Paris.
“Avoid the areas of the demonstrations,” the warning said.
Justice minister Gérald Darmanin announced 2,513 people had been taken into custody and 67 people had been imprisoned since the violence that marred the demonstrations this weekend, Liberation reported.
Here is the decree from the Paris police prefecture on the curfew which will be from 11 pm until 6am.
“The central median of the Place de la République” and “an area [...] delimited by the following squares and streets within it: Place Maurice-Quentin; Rue Berger from Place Maurice-Quentin to the corner of Boulevard Sébastopol; the section of Passage des Lingères that leads onto Rue Berger; Boulevard Sébastopol from the corner of Rue Berger to the corner of Allée André-Breton; Allée André-Breton.”
The prefecture clarifies that “residents who can prove, by any means, that their residence is located within the aforementioned areas, workers [...], members of the public emergency services, and shopkeepers are not subject to” the decree.
Demonstrations will also be prohibited from 8pm to 6am in other parts of the capital, such as Bastille, Châtelet, or near places of power like the Elysée, Matignon, the National Assembly and the Senate.
Eric Ciotti, the mayor of the southern French city of Nice, has also issued a curfew “to protect the people of Nice” starting from Monday evening 9pm local time to 6am. The curfew will remain in effect each night until Sunday, and will only apply to minors, he said.
According to Libération, only certain areas of the city are affected: the city center, Old Nice, the Trachel district, and the Gare du Sud (southern train station).
French authorities announce curfew for some parts of Paris and other cities
French authorities have issued an overnight curfew, which will come into effect from 11pm until 6am local time, for Place de la Republique and the streets around Les Halles inParis, according to Libération and France24.
The measure will apply to three categories of people: unaccompanied minors, people wearing personal protective equipment, and those concealing their faces.
Authorities had earlier issued the country’s first curfew to run for two days starting on Monday in the northern city of Lille and surrounding cities of Douai, Wattignies and Denain, France24 reported citing prime minister Sébastien Lecornu’s office.
The prefect of the Nord department has issued an order imposing a curfew for minors starting at 8 p.m. local time in certain areas of the cities of Lille, Douai, Wattignies, and Denain.
“These orders are issued in close collaboration with the mayors concerned,” the prefecture said.
The Prime Minister’s office stated the measure is in effect for Monday and Tuesday nights, from 8pm to 6 am, Liberation reported.
In Coulaines, a town of 8,000 inhabitants near Le Mans, the mayor, Christophe Rouillon, also announced on Facebook that he would be implementing a curfew “in the evening for minors who go out alone ,” starting at 11 p.m. on Monday.
The right-wing mayor of a town in Maine-et-Loire has decided to fly the flags at the town hall at half-mast and remove the portrait of Emmanuel Macron following the demonstrations in France.
“I condemn in the strongest possible terms the violence and damage committed by those who flout our laws, vandalise our towns, and show contempt for the values of the Republic,” Frédéric Mortier, the mayor of Longué-Jumelles, said.
“France cannot accept that some refuse common rules, reject the requirements of integration and challenge the authority of the State,” he continued.
The mayor added that he had also decided “to take down the portrait of the President of the Republic in the town hall”, explaining that the attitude of the head of state “in the face of this situation is unworthy of the gravity of the events and the expectations of our fellow citizens”.
France protests escalate with riots, looting and 2,400 arrests - podcast
Last weekend there were mass protests across France, with more than half a million people estimated to have been involved. The unrest included rioting, looting and violent clashes with outnumbered police in cities including Paris, Marseille and Limoges. The interior minister conceded that police “lost control” in some cities, while President Emmanuel Macron demanded a full security review.
For today’s instalment of The Latest podcast, Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s Europe correspondent, Jon Henley:
François Gatel, Minister for Territorial Collectivities, told the National Assembly there will be “the mobilisation of an exceptional fund to support the reconstruction of public facilities.”
He added it will be “a one-stop shop to support disaster-stricken communities” to coordinate and facilitate the process. The minister also promised regulatory “flexibilities” to ease the work.
Four police officers were injured and a police station was vandalised in the Garenne district of La Roche-sur-Yon by “around sixty individuals dressed in black and wearing balaclavas” who fired fireworks and other projectiles, Liberation reported.
‘It looks like a war zone’: France reels as looting continues for second night
Angelique Chrisafis
in Paris
Just before 1am on Monday morning, two motorbikes carrying one passenger each stopped at a traffic light on a backstreet near rue de Rivoli,one of central Paris’s busiest shopping streets.
“You’ve got to go where there are a lot of people, where they’ve done the shop windows,” said one motorbike rider to another. Minutes later 10 other men, their faces covered with ski balaclavas, came down the street on foot pursued by a police van.
Soon after Emmanuel Macron’stelevised speech on Sunday night telling the nation it was “unbearable to see our streets ransacked”, groups of men looted shops in central Paris for hours for a second night running. Dozens of people attempted to smash windows near Les Halles shopping centre and grab goods. Others broke into an electrical shop in Belleville in the north of the city.
“Men were battering shop windows, trying to break in, then they were chased by police,” said a 73-year-old woman near Les Halles.
“There were different groups running everywhere with police chasing on foot or by car, and at the same time, some people were setting bins and bikes alight. The groups breaking into shops aren’t hostile to passersby so you’d see local residents walking down the street on their way home late at night, and masked teenagers running past in the other direction carrying looted goods. It’s so strange – it’s like two different universes in parallel worlds.”
She said:
“It says a lot about society – it shows we have neglected our education system and that we’re living in a consumer society where all we say to our young people is: ‘buy, buy, buy’. In this type of extreme capitalism, some people don’t have enough money to buy all of this and so they attack.”
Macron begins Gulf trip aimed at securing petrol, diesel supplies
Meanwhile, as France was busy cleaning up its streets, the country’s president Emmanuel Macron – who last night delivered an address to the nation on the events – arrived in Kuwait for a Gulf trip aimed at securing additional petrol and diesel supplies to bring down pump prices, Reuters reported.
During the trip, he is also visiting the United Arab Emirates.
description: This live blog is now closed.Macron criticises ‘unbridled violence’ after 2,400 arrests across FranceFrench PM Lecornu says he has asked prefects to implement “a number of partial curfews” in certain “localised” urban areas to stop further disorder, which he attributes to “the extreme-left” and some criminal elements.We will no doubt hear more on this from local authorities, as in the example of Marseille (10:32). Continue reading...
author: Lucy Campbell, Nadeem Badshah, Jakub Krupa and Martin Belam
content:
Partial curfews have been issued for a number of French cities, including parts of Paris, after the government admitted police had “lost control” during violent weekend protests around the country. An overnight curfew will come into effect from 11pm until 6am local time, for Place de la Republique and the streets around Les Halles in Paris. Authorities earlier issued the country’s first curfew the northern city of Lille and surrounding cities of Douai, Wattignies and Denain. Curfews were also announced in the southern cities of Nice (specifically for minors) and central Lyon, while Marseille, earlier announced independently that it had banned all gatherings and demonstrations on Monday.
It came after France’s PM, Sébastien Lecornu, said after an emergency cabinet meeting that he was “fully resolved to restore public order” and had called for “local and partial” curfews if needed. There was “no question” of imposing a full curfew on entire cities, he said. Lecornu told reporters that if declaring a state of emergency was deemed necessary “we could do so”, but added that at this stage partial curfews seemed “more appropriate”.
France’s interior minister conceded that police had “lost control” in some cities during Saturday’s protests and the president, Emmanuel Macron, demanded a full security review and “new operational methods” to end the rioting. Laurent Nuñez said there had been a “lack of anticipation” in preparations for the protests and acknowledged that police numbers had sometimes been inadequate to deal with rioters and looters on the fringes of the demonstrations. Nuñez said intelligence had suggested there would be 200,000 demonstrators around the country. In the event, there were more than half a million and peaceful protests were hijacked, morphing into one of France’s most violent days of unrest in recent years. Almost 2,400 arrests have been made.
Nuñez said he had offered his resignation to Macron because he felt “responsible for everything that happened”, but the president had refused it, demanding instead that Nuñez “take all necessary steps to ensure transparency over planning and intelligence failures”. “You couldn’t look shopkeepers in the eye after hundreds of shops had been looted and say we hadn’t lost control,” the minister told French radio, but added that the responsibility of “rioters, looters and ultra-left militants” should not be glossed over.
The original protests, led by students, teachers, parents, unions and workers, focused on the high cost of living, an issue that also prompted demonstrations in several other European countries including Italy, Belgium and Albania over the weekend.
Trump refuses to drop false immigration claim when asked about France protests
Shrai Popat
Ahead of leaving for a campaign rally in Wichita, Kansas, Donald Trumpagain claimed – without evidence – that the riots throughout France are due to mass migration.
“I told Emmanuel [Macron], you should close up your borders,” the US president said. “I’ve known him for probably eight or nine years. I told him as soon as I met him, I said, ‘you’re making a big mistake’. We closed our borders. He didn’t.”
Analysis: Ferocious criticism from all sides underlines Macron’s isolation
Jon Henley
in Paris
The near-universal chorus of condemnation that greeted Emmanuel Macron’s address to the nation on Sunday, after one of the most violent days of rioting and looting in France’s recent history, was a stark reflection of just how weakened he now is.
A month-long protest by high school pupils over crumbling and crowded classrooms converged with broader frustrations over soaring living costs, rapidly widening inequality and falling public spending, bringing together students, teachers, trade unionists and a resurrected gilets jaunes movement.
Those largely peaceful protests were swiftly hijacked by masked groups who torched vehicles, ransacked businesses and severely damaged public infrastructure, including setting fire to Limoges’ city hall and invading that of Marseille.
Macron acknowledged the “deep anxiety” of young people but offered no concrete policy initiatives, no cabinet reshuffle and no new public spending, merely telling his prime minister to organise consultations and asking opposition politicians to take a stand.
The response, across the political spectrum, was damning. The Greens’ leader, Marine Tondelier, said that rather than “even beginning to make any kind of mea culpa”, Macron was “summoning us to the PM’s office like pupils to the blackboard”.
On the far right, the National Rally’s Jordan Bardella called the speech “lamentable” and said Macron had “nothing left to say” to the French. The party’s figurehead, Marine Le Pen, said the country was “caught in a vice between violence and impotence”.
The centre-right’s Bruno Retailleau said Macron was “totally overwhelmed”, while on the radical left, Jean-Luc Mélenchon accused the president of relying on “inaction and police brutality” in doomed hopes that the protests would simply fizzle out.
Perhaps most damagingly, even Macron’s former prime minister Édouard Philippe said he would have preferred “decisions and initiatives that might lead to a return to order and the restoration of state authority … Our country needs to be governed.”
Criticism is to be expected from rivals positioning themselves six months before a presidential election to choose Macron’s successor. But its sheer ferocity underlines his isolation, the disdain in which he is held, and the anger he inspires.
It’s a structural trap that he has largely set for himself. Macron came to power in 2017 as a “Jupiterian” president – a deliberate strategy aimed at elevating the head of state above daily politics, projecting distant authority and technocratic brilliance.
But over nine years in the Élysée, that high-handed style – partly born, his critics say, of Macron’s complete lack of basic political experience as an elected official in a town hall or as a constituency MP – has morphed into perceived arrogance and detachment.
It has been compounded by catastrophic strategic errors, and France’s spiralling economic problems. Macron lost a functional parliamentary majority by refusing to meaningfully campaign between the presidential and legislative elections of 2022.
Two years later he dissolved the national assembly. That gamble backfired spectacularly, with voters returning an even more deadlocked parliament split between a divided left, a much-diminished centrist bloc and Le Pen’s far right.
Without a working majority, the government repeatedly resorted to controversial constitutional manoeuvres to force through laws without a parliamentary vote, laying it – and Macron – open to further accusations of democratic illegitimacy.
Compounding that institutional deadlock is a looming fiscal crisis. In decades gone by, French presidents facing mass protests on the streets could in effect buy a degree of social tranquility with targeted spending packages or public sector concessions.
But France’s national debt, at 119% of GDP, is at its highest level since 1946. Its budget deficit, at 5.1%, is also among the highest in the EU. There is just no money in the bank to ease the cost of living squeeze that brought 550,000 people on to the streets on Saturday.
The markets are worried: France’s borrowing costs are higher than Greece’s. And with few fiscal options, the government’s clearest response – in time-honoured French tradition – has been teargas and baton charges, sometimes against schoolchildren, further aggravating tensions.
The consequences for the presidential election could be profound. The centrist coalition built around Macron’s brand has all but collapsed. If the protests and violence persist, the main beneficiary will be the law-and-order champions of the far right.
US advises Americans to avoid protest areas in France
The US state department has issued an alert warning Americans to avoid demonstration areas in major French cities after days of violent protests that have rocked the country.
The alert issued by the US embassy in Paris noted violent demonstrations on 17 October and the new curfews planned in cities including Lille and Paris.
“Avoid the areas of the demonstrations,” the warning said.
Justice minister Gérald Darmanin announced 2,513 people had been taken into custody and 67 people had been imprisoned since the violence that marred the demonstrations this weekend, Liberation reported.
Here is the decree from the Paris police prefecture on the curfew which will be from 11 pm until 6am.
“The central median of the Place de la République” and “an area [...] delimited by the following squares and streets within it: Place Maurice-Quentin; Rue Berger from Place Maurice-Quentin to the corner of Boulevard Sébastopol; the section of Passage des Lingères that leads onto Rue Berger; Boulevard Sébastopol from the corner of Rue Berger to the corner of Allée André-Breton; Allée André-Breton.”
The prefecture clarifies that “residents who can prove, by any means, that their residence is located within the aforementioned areas, workers [...], members of the public emergency services, and shopkeepers are not subject to” the decree.
Demonstrations will also be prohibited from 8pm to 6am in other parts of the capital, such as Bastille, Châtelet, or near places of power like the Elysée, Matignon, the National Assembly and the Senate.
Eric Ciotti, the mayor of the southern French city of Nice, has also issued a curfew “to protect the people of Nice” starting from Monday evening 9pm local time to 6am. The curfew will remain in effect each night until Sunday, and will only apply to minors, he said.
According to Libération, only certain areas of the city are affected: the city center, Old Nice, the Trachel district, and the Gare du Sud (southern train station).
French authorities announce curfew for some parts of Paris and other cities
French authorities have issued an overnight curfew, which will come into effect from 11pm until 6am local time, for Place de la Republique and the streets around Les Halles inParis, according to Libération and France24.
The measure will apply to three categories of people: unaccompanied minors, people wearing personal protective equipment, and those concealing their faces.
Authorities had earlier issued the country’s first curfew to run for two days starting on Monday in the northern city of Lille and surrounding cities of Douai, Wattignies and Denain, France24 reported citing prime minister Sébastien Lecornu’s office.
The prefect of the Nord department has issued an order imposing a curfew for minors starting at 8 p.m. local time in certain areas of the cities of Lille, Douai, Wattignies, and Denain.
“These orders are issued in close collaboration with the mayors concerned,” the prefecture said.
The Prime Minister’s office stated the measure is in effect for Monday and Tuesday nights, from 8pm to 6 am, Liberation reported.
In Coulaines, a town of 8,000 inhabitants near Le Mans, the mayor, Christophe Rouillon, also announced on Facebook that he would be implementing a curfew “in the evening for minors who go out alone ,” starting at 11 p.m. on Monday.
The right-wing mayor of a town in Maine-et-Loire has decided to fly the flags at the town hall at half-mast and remove the portrait of Emmanuel Macron following the demonstrations in France.
“I condemn in the strongest possible terms the violence and damage committed by those who flout our laws, vandalise our towns, and show contempt for the values of the Republic,” Frédéric Mortier, the mayor of Longué-Jumelles, said.
“France cannot accept that some refuse common rules, reject the requirements of integration and challenge the authority of the State,” he continued.
The mayor added that he had also decided “to take down the portrait of the President of the Republic in the town hall”, explaining that the attitude of the head of state “in the face of this situation is unworthy of the gravity of the events and the expectations of our fellow citizens”.
France protests escalate with riots, looting and 2,400 arrests - podcast
Last weekend there were mass protests across France, with more than half a million people estimated to have been involved. The unrest included rioting, looting and violent clashes with outnumbered police in cities including Paris, Marseille and Limoges. The interior minister conceded that police “lost control” in some cities, while President Emmanuel Macron demanded a full security review.
For today’s instalment of The Latest podcast, Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s Europe correspondent, Jon Henley:
François Gatel, Minister for Territorial Collectivities, told the National Assembly there will be “the mobilisation of an exceptional fund to support the reconstruction of public facilities.”
He added it will be “a one-stop shop to support disaster-stricken communities” to coordinate and facilitate the process. The minister also promised regulatory “flexibilities” to ease the work.
Four police officers were injured and a police station was vandalised in the Garenne district of La Roche-sur-Yon by “around sixty individuals dressed in black and wearing balaclavas” who fired fireworks and other projectiles, Liberation reported.
‘It looks like a war zone’: France reels as looting continues for second night
Angelique Chrisafis
in Paris
Just before 1am on Monday morning, two motorbikes carrying one passenger each stopped at a traffic light on a backstreet near rue de Rivoli,one of central Paris’s busiest shopping streets.
“You’ve got to go where there are a lot of people, where they’ve done the shop windows,” said one motorbike rider to another. Minutes later 10 other men, their faces covered with ski balaclavas, came down the street on foot pursued by a police van.
Soon after Emmanuel Macron’stelevised speech on Sunday night telling the nation it was “unbearable to see our streets ransacked”, groups of men looted shops in central Paris for hours for a second night running. Dozens of people attempted to smash windows near Les Halles shopping centre and grab goods. Others broke into an electrical shop in Belleville in the north of the city.
“Men were battering shop windows, trying to break in, then they were chased by police,” said a 73-year-old woman near Les Halles.
“There were different groups running everywhere with police chasing on foot or by car, and at the same time, some people were setting bins and bikes alight. The groups breaking into shops aren’t hostile to passersby so you’d see local residents walking down the street on their way home late at night, and masked teenagers running past in the other direction carrying looted goods. It’s so strange – it’s like two different universes in parallel worlds.”
She said:
“It says a lot about society – it shows we have neglected our education system and that we’re living in a consumer society where all we say to our young people is: ‘buy, buy, buy’. In this type of extreme capitalism, some people don’t have enough money to buy all of this and so they attack.”
Macron begins Gulf trip aimed at securing petrol, diesel supplies
Meanwhile, as France was busy cleaning up its streets, the country’s president Emmanuel Macron – who last night delivered an address to the nation on the events – arrived in Kuwait for a Gulf trip aimed at securing additional petrol and diesel supplies to bring down pump prices, Reuters reported.
During the trip, he is also visiting the United Arab Emirates.

title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
content_c:
The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
October 19, 2026
There's a lot of stopping and staring in Knightsbridge. This part of central London is within a stone's throw of Buckingham Palace, Hyde Park and Harrods, bringing inquisitive tourists in droves.
While it may not divert quite as many eyeballs as the seat of the British monarchy, a curious collection of plants, garden umbrellas, shopping bags and children's toys filling a building's entrance causes many a curious glance.
The peculiar arrangement on a grand portico is what Anders Fernstedt, a man from Sweden who fell on hard times, has been calling home for more than three years already.
That building hosting his makeshift setup was, just a few years ago, London's most expensive house.
The mega-mansion at 2-8A Rutland Gate sold in 2020 for a then-record £210 million (€244 million, $278 million) to Hui Ka Yan, the founder of China's Evergrande group, who was sentenced to life in prison last month.
Hui never moved in and the house was registered under his wife's name. The freezing of her assets means it can't be seized by liquidators and the house is in a state of limbo.
So too was Fernstedt when he first stumbled across it. "I just thought, it would be a shelter for the night. I'm an avid camper, like an amateur botanist. I'm not afraid of nature," he told DW.
'Camping on the balcony'
Fernstedt has never been inside the property, which appears to be in a state of disrepair. Instead, he gradually built his home in the portico, where grand columns guard the 45 rooms, indoor swimming pool and 116 windows. Year round he sleeps under the portico roof and a large umbrella which provides a hidden nook in which he's placed mattresses and bedding.
"I haven't had a bad night's sleep for as long as I can remember. And that goes for four seasons. It's not cold in the winter, and because I don't have walls, I get the breeze in the heat," he said.
"My conceit when I started was that sort of fake dream. Oh, I'm just a boy, my parents are in the house, everything's normal, I just asked them for permission to camp on the balcony."
Fernstedt was raised by his mother in Sweden before embarking on a range of careers at home and in the US, building a name for himself in the tech world.
In 2016, he moved to England where he worked as a journalist and fact checker at publications including The Economist, before work dried up around the time of the COVID pandemic.
A share in a tech company from his days in the US gave Anders a nest egg he relied on. But it couldn't last forever and he found himself living in a tent and then temporary accommodation, where he experienced violence and brushed up against people with severe addictions.
"Perhaps in this contemporary world, the biggest curiosity about my lifestyle is I'm completely off money," he said.
Community support powers unusual lifestyle
Fernstedt has built relationships with bakeries, cafes and florists in which he gets unused food, flowers for his home and use of power. He also makes use of a homeless charity in nearby Victoria for showers, clothing donations and socializing. But he's also made himself a broadly accepted part of one of London's most affluent neighborhoods.
"This is a very sophisticated neighborhood. I'd stayed for a few weeks and I knew everybody knew that I was here. And I thought, how can I sort of convey my presence without being present? And I thought, my constituency has to be the neighbors' children and grandchildren. Because if they plead my case at the kitchen table, my prospects improve," he said, by way of explaining the toys that line his abode.
"It is, in a way, a squirrel's nut collection," he added, when asked if he's worried about leaving his possessions out in the open. "I have so many nuts that I won't notice when something disappears."
There are some neighbors who do object to his presence, but Anders does his best to keep his home neat and his life quiet. Indeed, many others feel his presence prevents the house being a target for thieves or vandals. Overall though, he's found the community welcoming.
"Sometimes they introduce themselves asking what might I want or need. And my stock answer being: 'well, what you just gave me, a little bit of normal time, right? And neighborly banter'," he said. "Sometimes I'll be given food and very elegant Italian dinner jackets and clothes have arrived on a few occasions."
Homelessness a growing concern in London
Not all homeless people in London have found such a stable lifestyle. Homeless charity Crisis estimates that there are over 200,000 people classified as homeless in England's capital, where "4,392 people were recorded sleeping rough in London between April and June, up from 4% on the same time last year. This is up 58% compared to 10 years ago."
According to government figures, there were 105,138 empty homes in London in 2025, or 1 in every 37 homes. Andy Burnham, who became British Prime Minister in July, has since vowed to offer "every rough sleeper in England a route off the streets by Christmas."
With such an enormous price tag, even after six years of being abandoned, Fernstedt knows that the house he lives at could potentially become untenable at virtually any moment.
But over the last few years, it's given him something he craved when pitching up his tent or being moved from one scary temporary residence to the next.
"I'm no longer really worried that I'll cycle around the corner and everything will be gone. Because I've been here so long, I'm free of worrying now, and if we worry too much, we won't be happy."
Edited by: Elizabeth Grenier

title: Peter Christian Zinkann: Langjähriger Miele-Chef ist tot
content_c:
Peter Christian Zinkann Langjähriger Miele-Chef ist tot
Der frühere Chef der Firma Miele, Peter Christian Zinkann, ist tot. Er starb am Montag im Alter von 98 Jahren, wie das Unternehmen in Gütersloh mitteilte . Mit seinem Tod »verlieren Miele, die Industrie und das Land eine herausragende Unternehmerpersönlichkeit, die Familie ihren großmütigen Patriarchen, die Stadt einen engagierten Ehrenbürger – und die Belegschaft von Miele ihren hochverehrten Seniorchef«.
Behalten Sie den Überblick: Jeden Werktag gegen 18 Uhr beantworten SPIEGEL-Autorinnen und -Autoren die wichtigsten Fragen des Tages im Newsletter »Die Lage am Abend« – hintergründig, kompakt, kostenlos. Hier bestellen Sie Ihr News-Briefing als Mail.
Zinkann kam 1928 in Bremen zur Welt. 1945 zog er mit seiner Familie nach Gütersloh. Nach einem Maschinenbaustudium samt Promotion startete er den Angaben zufolge 1958 bei der Firma, die sein Großvater Reinhard Zinkann gemeinsam mit Carl Miele 1899 gegründet hatte. Mehr als vier Jahrzehnte lang leitete er die Firma zusammen mit seinem Geschäftspartner Rudolf Miele. Dieser starb 2004. Im selben Jahr schied Zinkann als geschäftsführender Gesellschafter aus.
Sein Sohn Reinhard Zinkann ist seit 1999 Mitglied der Miele-Geschäftsleitung.
Rudolf Miele und Peter Christian Zinkann (2000 in einer Ausstellungsküche in Gütersloh)
Foto:
IMAGO
Mit Blick auf das Leben von Peter Christian Zinkann würdigte das Unternehmen seine »entscheidende Rolle« beim Erfolg von Miele. In Zinkanns Zeit brachte das mittelständische Unternehmen etwa einen elektronisch gesteuerten Trockner (1966) auf den Markt, Spülmaschinen mit Besteckschubladen (ab 1986) und die Miele-Schontrommel (2001).
Miele kam im vergangenen Jahr eigenen Angaben zufolge auf einen Umsatz von 5,16 Milliarden Euro und damit 2,3 Prozent mehr als 2024. Zum Gewinn macht die Firma mit ihren rund 23.000 Beschäftigten keine Angaben. Das Unternehmen stellt Waschmaschinen, Trockner, Spülmaschinen, Kaffee-Vollautomaten, Staubsauger und weitere Haushaltsgeräte her.
Reinhard Zinkann, Urenkel eines Gründers und Co-Chef des deutschen Hausgeräteherstellers Miele, hat Jobs nach Polen verlagert und einen Standort in Alabama eröffnet. Im Mai 2025 sprach er mit dem SPIEGEL über die Gründe – das Gespräch können Sie hier nachlesen .
description: Sein Großvater hatte die Firma Miele einst mitgegründet, Peter Christian Zinkann selbst leitete sie mehr als vier Jahrzehnte lang. Nun trauert der Haushaltsgerätehersteller um eine »herausragende Unternehmerpersönlichkeit«.

title: Auschwitz-Überlebender Höllenreiner im Alter von 92 gestorben
content_c:
Im Alter von 92 Jahren Auschwitz-Überlebender Höllenreiner gestorben
Hermann Höllenreiner überlebte das Vernichtungslager Auschwitz - und floh im Alter von elf Jahren von einem der Todesmärsche. Mit 92 Jahren ist er nun gestorben.
Der Auschwitz-Überlebende Hermann Höllenreiner ist im Alter von 92 Jahren gestorben. Das teilten der Hanser Verlag in München und das Internationale Auschwitz Komitee mit. Demnach starb er am 16. Oktober im oberbayerischen Mettenheim bei Mühldorf am Inn im Kreise seiner Familie.
Höllenreiner - von seiner Familie Mano genannt - stammte aus einer großen bayerischen Sinti-Familie. Im Alter von neun Jahren wurde er deportiert. Im Januar 1945 gelang es ihm, auf einem der Todesmärsche zu fliehen. Damals war er elf Jahre alt. Neben dem Vernichtungslager Auschwitz-Birkenau überlebte er auch die Lager Ravensbrück und Sachsenhausen.
"Ein großer Zeitzeuge"
"Erst spät in seinem Leben begann er zu erzählen und wurde ein großer Zeitzeuge, der von den Schrecken von Auschwitz, von den Tätern und Opfern, vor allem aber von der immer noch andauernden Diskriminierung der Sinti und Roma in Europa eindringlich berichtete", würdigte Christoph Heubner, der Exekutiv-Vizepräsident des Internationalen Auschwitz Komitees, den Verstorbenen. Höllenreiner wurde 2013 mit dem Bundesverdienstkreuz ausgezeichnet.

title: Від ранку РФ атакує захід України реактивними БпЛА: де є загроза - мапа
content_c:
Від ранку РФ атакує захід України реактивними БпЛА: де є загроза — мапа
Російська армія атакує Україну реактивними дронами — повітряна тривога охопила низку регіонів.
Від самого ранку 20 жовтня російська армія атакує Україну ударними безпілотниками, зокрема реактивними. Повітряні Сили ЗСУ повідомляють про рух ворожих БпЛА одразу в кількох областях.
Що відомо про рух ударних БпЛА — читайте у матеріалі ТСН.ua.
Вночі російська армія атакувала Україну безпілотниками. У різних регіонах України працювали сили ППО. Зранку атака триває. Зокрема, ворожі цілі фіксують на підступах до західних областей.
Нічна атака — звіт Повітряних сил
У ранковому звіті військові повідомили, що від вечора 19 жовтня армія РФ із семи напрямків запустила по Україні 165 ударних БпЛА типу Shahed, з яких 105 — реактивні. Також летіли S8000 Бандероль/Дань-Т, Гербера, дрони-імітатори типу «Пародія».
За попередніми даними, станом на 08:00, було збито/подавлено 115 БпЛА, зокрема 73 реактивних. 
Водночас сталось влучання на 30 локаціях, а також падіння уламків зафіксували на 13 локаціях.
Вранішня атака
Станом на 08:55 безпілотники тримають рух на захід, однак сирени у регіонах поки не лунають. Тривогу жовтого рівня оголошено у частині західних, північних і південних областей, а також в центрі.
Крім того, існує загроза для Києва. Столиця «пожовтіла» о 08:38, пролунали сильні вибухи. За даними Повітряних Сил ЗСУ, дрони рухалися в напрямку Лісового масиву, Русанівки, Деміївки, Караваєвих Дач і Святошина. Також безпілотники прямували до Чайок і Макарова на Київщині.
Крім того, реактивні БпЛА фіксували на Вінниччині, Полтавщині, Черкащині, Миколаївщині тощо.
За даними Повітряних сил, станом на 07:00 російські реактивні безпілотники рухалися у напрямку західних областей. Зокрема, БпЛА фіксували у Вінницькій, Хмельницькій, Рівненській, Тернопільській, Волинській, Львівській та Івано-Франківській областях.
Крім того, дрони фіксували у напрямку Вишгорода та Бучі у Київській області, на Харківщині, Кіровоградщині, Вінниччині, Миколаївщині та Полтавщині.
Нагадаємо, військовий експерт Олег Жданов вважає, що Росія може повторювати комбіновані атаки по Україні з інтервалом у три-чотири доби. Водночас більш звичним для російської армії темпом може бути один такий удар на тиждень. Експерт наголосив, що йдеться саме про комбіновані атаки, під час яких РФ одночасно застосовує ударні безпілотники і ракети.

title: Администрация Трампа задерживает одобрение передачи ракет Patriot Украине — WP
content_c:
Администрация президента Соединенных Штатов Дональда Трампа задерживает согласование передачи Украине ракет-перехватчиков Patriot от стран-партнеров. Министр войны США Пит Хегсет до сих пор не завершил необходимые для этого процедуры. Об этом сообщило издание The Washington Post.
По крайней мере часть запланированных поставок требует личного одобрения Хегсета. Вашингтон сохраняет такие полномочия, поскольку американское оружие поставляется за границу при условии, что его дальнейшая передача третьим странам будет происходить с разрешения США. Об этом рассказали американский чиновник и ещё трое собеседников издания, осведомлённых о ситуации.
Формального отказа со стороны Хегсета не было. В то же время он не предпринял необходимых шагов для одобрения этих поставок. Министр продолжает согласовывать отдельные виды американской помощи Украине. Задержки происходят в условиях острого дефицита перехватчиков. На прошлой неделе украинский чиновник сообщил изданию, что в украинских запасах осталась «всего пара» таких ракет.
Критическую нехватку боеприпасов для Patriot Украина испытывает еще с лета. Это ослабляет защиту населения от почти ежедневных российских баллистических атак. Перехватывать их без современных технологических средств чрезвычайно сложно. Война США против Ирана создала огромную нагрузку на мировые запасы перехватчиков Patriot. Украина теперь ежемесячно сталкивается с критической нехваткой.
Американская сторона обычно поставляет новые ракеты небольшими партиями по мере производства, нередко всего по несколько единиц. В то же время Киев и его партнеры ищут доступные запасы в других странах. Их призывают передать Украине те перехватчики, которые они могут выделить.
Проблемы с поставками сопровождаются повторными сбоями в системе раннего предупреждения о баллистических ударах. Она зависит от американских разведданных. В понедельник, 19 октября, Зеленский сообщил, что Россия вновь нанесла несколько волн ударов в течение ночи, а предупреждения от партнеров не поступало. По его словам, российские силы применили против Украины 16 баллистических ракет. Ситуацию, когда поставки ракет для украинской ПВО блокируются, а Россия получает ослабление или отсрочку санкций, Зеленский назвал отрицанием реальности со стороны партнеров.
Трамп в понедельник заявил, что США продолжают делиться разведданными с Украиной. Он несколько раз повторил, что Вашингтон оказал Киеву значительную помощь, и утверждал, что ничего не получил взамен. Государственный секретарь Марко Рубио в тот же день также опроверг наличие какой-либо паузы в обмене разведывательной информацией. Отвечая на вопросы журналистов во время визита в Узбекистан, он сказал, что Вашингтон хочет сосредоточиться на завершении войны. По его словам, именно на этом должен сосредоточиться и Зеленский.
На вопрос об отсутствии заблаговременных предупреждений о последних атаках Рубио ответил, что несколько ночей назад возникла «проблема с программным обеспечением». Ее, по его словам, изучает Европейское командование Вооруженных сил США. Для Украины доступ к американской разведке имеет важное значение, поскольку помогает выявлять ракетные удары.
В понедельник Зеленский провел групповую беседу с американскими сенаторами. Он обсудил трудности, с которыми Украина сталкивается из-за резкого ухудшения отношений с Трампом. Несколько влиятельных республиканцев в последнее время усилили критику уступок американского президента в адрес России. Особенно их возмутило пятничное решение не применять санкции, предусмотренные двухпартийным законом в честь покойного сенатора Линдси Грэма.
Председатель сенатского комитета по вооруженным силам, республиканец из Миссисипи Роджер Викер, в воскресенье обнародовал необычно прямое заявление с призывом к Трампу подтвердить поддержку Украины. Перед этим сенатор встретился с Зеленским в Киеве. По словам Викера, украинский президент готов прекратить атаки на российские НПЗ, если Россия остановит удары по украинской инфраструктуре. Сенатор заявил, что Трамп может снизить цены на топливо уже сейчас, просто согласившись на такую договоренность. Он призвал американского президента воспользоваться этой возможностью и одержать политическую победу.
Напомним, что Зеленский в интервью 18 октября заявил об американском давлении, которое, по его мнению, подталкивает Украину к капитуляции перед Россией. Он предложил прекратить удары по российским НПЗ в обмен на дополнительные ракеты для Patriot. По словам президента, Украина уже оплатила вооружение по программе PURL, однако США одобрили лишь часть поставок. Зеленский заявил, что Киев получает ежемесячно только 12 перехватчиков Patriot — примерно четверть от объемов при администрации Джо Байдена.
Кроме того, Трамп вновь обвинил Зеленского в якобы нежелании завершить войну. В посте в Truth Social он объяснил отказ подписать документ о санкциях против России стремлением удержать Москву за столом переговоров. Трамп заявил, что может подписать его позже, когда сочтёт нужным. Он также утверждал, что Россия помогает Ирану значительно меньше, чем могла бы, и выразил желание сохранить такое положение дел.
description: Пентагон до сих пор не завершил согласование мер, необходимых для усиления защиты от российских обстрелов.

Государственный секретарь Марко Рубио в тот же день также опроверг наличие какой-либо паузы в обмене разведывательной информацией. Отвечая на вопросы журналистов во время визита в Узбекистан, он сказал, что Вашингтон хочет сосредоточиться на завершении войны. По его словам, именно на этом должен сосредоточиться и Зеленский.
На вопрос об отсутствии заблаговременных предупреждений о последних атаках Рубио ответил, что несколько ночей назад возникла «проблема с программным обеспечением». Ее, по его словам, изучает Европейское командование Вооруженных сил США. Для Украины доступ к американской разведке имеет важное значение, поскольку помогает выявлять ракетные удары.
В понедельник Зеленский провел групповую беседу с американскими сенаторами. Он обсудил трудности, с которыми Украина сталкивается из-за резкого ухудшения отношений с Трампом. Несколько влиятельных республиканцев в последнее время усилили критику уступок американского президента в адрес России. Особенно их возмутило пятничное решение не применять санкции, предусмотренные двухпартийным законом в честь покойного сенатора Линдси Грэма.
Председатель сенатского комитета по вооруженным силам, республиканец из Миссисипи Роджер Викер, в воскресенье обнародовал необычно прямое заявление с призывом к Трампу подтвердить поддержку Украины. Перед этим сенатор встретился с Зеленским в Киеве. По словам Викера, украинский президент готов прекратить атаки на российские НПЗ, если Россия остановит удары по украинской инфраструктуре. Сенатор заявил, что Трамп может снизить цены на топливо уже сейчас, просто согласившись на такую договоренность. Он призвал американского президента воспользоваться этой возможностью и одержать политическую победу.
Напомним, что Зеленский в интервью 18 октября заявил об американском давлении, которое, по его мнению, подталкивает Украину к капитуляции перед Россией. Он предложил прекратить удары по российским НПЗ в обмен на дополнительные ракеты для Patriot. По словам президента, Украина уже оплатила вооружение по программе PURL, однако США одобрили лишь часть поставок. Зеленский заявил, что Киев получает ежемесячно только 12 перехватчиков Patriot — примерно четверть от объемов при администрации Джо Байдена.
Кроме того, Трамп вновь обвинил Зеленского в якобы нежелании завершить войну. В посте в Truth Social он объяснил отказ подписать документ о санкциях против России стремлением удержать Москву за столом переговоров. Трамп заявил, что может подписать его позже, когда сочтёт нужным. Он также утверждал, что Россия помогает Ирану значительно меньше, чем могла бы, и выразил желание сохранить такое положение дел.

title: Обмеження швидкості Starshield вплинуло на передачу даних українським бойовим вертольотам – Бескрестнов
content_c:
Обмеження швидкості супутникового зв'язку Starshield до 160 км/год вплинуло на важливий канал передачі інформації українським бойовим вертольотам, які використовують для перехоплення російських безпілотників типу "шахед", повідомив радник президента України з питань оборонних технологій Сергій Бескрестнов (Флеш).
"Значну частину звичайних "Шахедів" збивають наші вертольоти. Вертольоти літають швидше за 160 км/год. Обмеження швидкості Starshield вплинуло на важливий канал передачі інформації на бойові вертольоти", – написав він у Телеграмі у понеділок.
За словами Бескрестнова, обмеження швидкості супутникового зв'язку досі не скасовано. Раніше він повідомляв, що воно також унеможливлює використання українських реактивних перехоплювачів для боротьби з російськими реактивними "шахедами".
"Мені дуже важко усвідомлювати, що один раптовий крок партнерів руйнує значну частину нашої оборони", – зазначив він, висловивши сподівання, що ситуація є непорозумінням і її буде врегульовано.

title: Catalonia's former rebel president can return to Spain, court rules
content_c:
Catalonia's former rebel president can return to Spain, court rules
- Published
Spain's Supreme Court has ruled the former president of Catalonia, Carles Puigdemont, can return without fear of arrest nearly a decade after going into self-imposed exile having led a failed independence bid.
The court upheld a decision to lift an arrest warrant for him linked to the referendum his regional government organised in 2017, in defiance of Madrid.
Direct rule was imposed on the region soon after the vote and Puigdemont fled to Belgium, where he has been based ever since - with a surprise appearance in Barcelona in 2024 prompting a police manhunt.
But the Spain to which he may return is much different from a decade ago, with Catalan independence now a marginal political issue.
Monday's ruling brings to an end a lengthy legal wrangle between the Spanish judiciary and the former Catalan president.
In 2024, Spain's socialist government introduced a controversial amnesty for dozens of Catalan politicians and activists who were involved in the secession drive, but the Supreme Court said Puigdemont and several of his colleagues should be excluded.
It argued this was because of the charges against them of alleged financial crimes around staging the referendum.
The Constitutional Court overruled that interpretation earlier this month, and on Monday the Supreme Court rejected an appeal by the far-right Vox party against lifting national arrest warrants for Puigdemont, as well as his former ministers Lluís Puig and Toni Comín, paving the way for their return to Spain.
- Ex-Catalan leader ‘eludes police manhunt and flees Spain’ 
  - Published9 August 2024
- Catalonia's bid for independence from Spain explained 
  - Published18 October 2019
- Spanish PM Sánchez calls early election after housing protests 
  - Published5 October
Puigdemont was elected as a member of the European Parliament (MEP) in 2019 and to the Catalan parliament in 2024 as leader of the region's centre-right Together for Catalonia (JxCat) party.
He had campaigned in the south of France, where he held rallies attended by supporters who travelled across the border to see him.
Puigdemont is known to have made at least one brief return to Spain since leaving the country, addressing a crowd of supporters in Barcelona prior to disappearing and escaping back over the border to France before he could be detained.
While he was living in Waterloo, Belgium, nine of his former colleagues were jailed for their role in the events of 2017. They were released when the Spanish government pardoned them in 2021.
Puigdemont has remained an active political presence, travelling across Europe to espouse the Catalan independence cause and fiercely criticising Spain's democratic institutions.
In a video posted on social media just as the Supreme Court ruling was announced, Puigdemont spoke of his reasons for staying abroad.
"My role was to stir public opinion, internationalise the conflict and work from the heart of Europe to explain the reality of Spain," he said.
It is still not known when he might return to Spain.
Comín, his former regional minister for health, plans to travel this week to Madrid, where he is due to carry out administrative procedures linked to his status as an MEP.
The referendum sparked the country's biggest political crisis since democracy was restored following the death of Francisco Franco.
The banned vote was met with a heavy police crackdown. The region's separatist majority declared independence after the vote - Madrid then dissolved parliament, sacked its leaders and called a snap election.
But Catalan independence is now a relatively marginal issue in Spain, with housing and immigration dominating the political agenda.
The parliamentary support of Puigdemont's JxCat party was instrumental in allowing current Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez to form a new left-wing Spanish government after the 2023 election.
But within Catalonia, JxCat has been struggling, with a far-right, pro-independence party, Catalan Alliance, taking many of its voters.
And next month, Spain's general election could see the far right enter government for the first time.

title: ‘Crucial opportunity to act’ as study finds most of Europe’s wild bee species in decline
content_c:
Most of Europe’s wild bee species and about half of its hover fly species have declined over the last century, a study has found, as a UN biodiversity summit begins in Armenia.
Records since 1921 show more bee species are declining than increasing in all parts of Europe except the Alpine region. The richness of bee and hover fly species suffered a persistent drop in the Atlantic and Continental regions, the study found, though trends in other regions were mixed or even positive.
The data, which covers 88% of bee and hover fly species across the continent, suggests pollinator communities have been reshaped by the “gradual loss of sensitive species and the rise of a resilient few”, according to the scientists. They warned of “deeper functional disruptions” if existing trends were not addressed.
Nearly 90% of wild flowering plants, as well as more than three-quarters of major food crop types, depend in part on animal pollination. The UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization has warned the decline of pollinators sets off a chain reaction that threatens wildlife and weakens the ability of ecosystems to withstand climate change and environmental stress.
Carlos Martínez-Núñez, an ecologist at the Spanish National Research Council and lead author of the study, said the findings showed that biodiversity loss could remain hidden behind apparently stable species numbers, “giving us a crucial opportunity to act before further declines occur”.
“The fact that some species are increasing today does not mean they will remain winners as climate change and habitat loss intensify,” he added.
The findings come as diplomats gather in Yerevan for the 17th UN conference on biodiversity. The summit, known as Cop17, will focus on the conservation and sustainable use of the natural world, and the shared benefits of its genetic resources.
The study found 91% of the species logged over the last century had also been recorded at least once in the modern period, between 2001 and 2020. Although this suggests as many as 9% of species could have been wiped out in Europe, many of the species not spotted recently occur only rarely in the historical record, and the researchers said they “do not expect widespread extinctions to have occurred yet”.
However, the species’ occupancy – the probability of being found at a given site – had mostly fallen.
Ainhoa Magrach, an environmental researcher at the Basque Centre for Climate Change (BC3), who was not involved in the study, said it “confirms what has long been suspected: many pollinator species are losing populations, and the decline is not affecting all of them equally”.
“Until now, most of the evidence came from a few north-western European countries, such as the UK, Belgium and the Netherlands,” she said. “This work shows that the pattern extends across the continent, although some regional differences exist.”
Wildlife is dying out at an unprecedented rate as humans destroy habitats, spray pesticides, and warp the weather with planet-heating pollution. Despite far-reaching consequences for humanity, including threats to food systems and further breakdown of the climate, governments have not met a single UN target on nature since the biodiversity convention was created in Rio in 1992.
The Cop17 summit is expected to focus on assessing progress toward this decade’s targets, which include protecting 30% of land and sea, reforming $500bn (£375bn) of environmentally damaging subsidies and restoring 30% of the planet’s degraded ecosystems.

title: Greece: At least 12 die in migrant drownings overnight
content_c:
Greece: At least 12 people die in migrant boat accidents overnight
October 19, 2026
Greek Coast Guard officials say 12 migrants were killed in the Aegean Sea overnight in two separate boating accidents.
In the first incident, six people — four men, a woman and an infant — were killed in waters off the coast of Lesbos when "a speedboat carrying migrants collided with the port side of a police patrol vessel," according to the Coast Guard.
Eight people were reported rescued.
In the second incident, six people — five men and a woman — drowned after their boat capsized off the coast of Samos, while 14 were rescued.
A search-and-rescue mission is ongoing in the area.
Authorities say they arrested a 37-year-old Turkish national among the survivors in the first incident, identifying him as a suspected smuggler and the operator of the speedboat.
Greece's Minister of Shipping and Island Policy Vassilis Kikilias blamed migrant traffickers for all of the deaths, posting on X, "Our position is non-negotiable: Zero tolerance for smugglers."
Turkey to Greece: Deadly migrant passage to Europe
Greece has long been a gateway to Europe for migrants and refugees from the Middle East, Africa and Asia who usually set off on the notoriously deadly sea voyage from Turkey.
According to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), refugee arrivals in Greece are declining this year.
As of October 11, 2026, some 25,000 arrivals had been recorded compared to 42,000 in 2025.
Almost one million migrants and refugees landed on Greece's shores during the 2015/2016 migration crisis, here, too, mainly from Turkey.
Edited by: Karl Sexton

title: Iran: Spionageurteile belasten Verhältnis – Botschafter einbestellt
content_c:
Diplomatische Spannungen Iran bestellt deutschen Botschafter ein
Im Streit mit Deutschland hat Iran den deutschen Botschafter Axel Dittmann einbestellt. Ihm sollte der Protest Teherans gegen die »verächtliche Haltung bestimmter deutscher Amtsträger« übermittelt werden, berichtet der iranische Staatssender Press TV unter Berufung auf einen Vertreter des Außenministeriums.
Generaldirektor Aliresa Jussefi sagt demnach, die Vorwürfe gegen Iran seien ein Versuch, die deutsche Unterstützung für den Krieg der USA und Israels gegen das Land zu verschleiern. Wenige Stunden zuvor hatte das Auswärtige Amt den iranischen Botschafter einbestellt.
Anlass dafür waren die Urteile gegen zwei Männer, die nach Auffassung des Hanseatischen Oberlandesgerichts in Hamburg im Auftrag des iranischen Geheimdienstes tätig waren. Das Gericht verurteilte einen 54-Jährigen zu achteinhalb und einen 43-Jährigen zu viereinhalb Jahren Gefängnis.
Zwei Männer wegen Spionage verurteilt
Die beiden in Dänemark lebenden Männer sollen den Präsidenten des Zentralrats der Juden, Josef Schuster, und den Präsidenten der Deutsch-Israelischen Gesellschaft, Volker Beck, ausgespäht haben. Zudem ging es um eine versuchte Beteiligung an Mord und schwerer Brandstiftung.
Iran bestellt nach Angaben staatlicher Medien außerdem den EU-Botschafter in Teheran, den Iren Aidan Cronin, ein. Damit wolle die Regierung gegen eine Reihe von »grundlosen« Vorwürfen protestieren.
Jussefi machte die EU für die angespannte Lage in Westasien und am Persischen Golf mitverantwortlich. Die Situation sei das Ergebnis einer »verantwortungslosen Politik« der Europäischen Union. Irland hat derzeit den Vorsitz im Rat der EU inne.
description: Erst hat Berlin den iranischen Botschafter einbestellt, nun reagiert Teheran und bestellt den deutschen sowie den EU-Botschafter ein. Hintergrund sind Verurteilungen wegen Spionage für Iran.

Generaldirektor Aliresa Jussefi sagt demnach, die Vorwürfe gegen Iran seien ein Versuch, die deutsche Unterstützung für den Krieg der USA und Israels gegen das Land zu verschleiern. Wenige Stunden zuvor hatte das Auswärtige Amt den iranischen Botschafter einbestellt.
Anlass dafür waren die Urteile gegen zwei Männer, die nach Auffassung des Hanseatischen Oberlandesgerichts in Hamburg im Auftrag des iranischen Geheimdienstes tätig waren. Das Gericht verurteilte einen 54-Jährigen zu achteinhalb und einen 43-Jährigen zu viereinhalb Jahren Gefängnis.
Zwei Männer wegen Spionage verurteilt
Die beiden in Dänemark lebenden Männer sollen den Präsidenten des Zentralrats der Juden, Josef Schuster, und den Präsidenten der Deutsch-Israelischen Gesellschaft, Volker Beck, ausgespäht haben. Zudem ging es um eine versuchte Beteiligung an Mord und schwerer Brandstiftung.
Iran bestellt nach Angaben staatlicher Medien außerdem den EU-Botschafter in Teheran, den Iren Aidan Cronin, ein. Damit wolle die Regierung gegen eine Reihe von »grundlosen« Vorwürfen protestieren.
Jussefi machte die EU für die angespannte Lage in Westasien und am Persischen Golf mitverantwortlich. Die Situation sei das Ergebnis einer »verantwortungslosen Politik« der Europäischen Union. Irland hat derzeit den Vorsitz im Rat der EU inne.

title: Reiche verspricht Milliarden für Wasserstoff-Ausbau
content_c:
Neue Förderungen Reiche verspricht Milliarden für Wasserstoff-Ausbau
Der Markt für Wasserstoff kommt nur langsam in Gang. Wirtschaftsministerin Reiche will nun mit Milliardenhilfen für die Industrie und Anreizen für klimafreundlichen Stahl gegensteuern.
Bundeswirtschaftsministerin Katherina Reiche (CDU) will den schleppenden Aufbau des Wasserstoffmarktes in Deutschland mit einer Milliardenförderung und neuen Anreizen voranbringen. Ihr Ministerium stellte dazu in Berlin ein Paket mit zehn Maßnahmen vor.
Kernstück ist eine Förderung von mindestens 1,5 Milliarden Euro für Industrieunternehmen, die ihre Produktion auf Wasserstoff umstellen. Zudem soll die Umrüstung von Gaskraftwerken auf Wasserstoff unterstützt und die Nachfrage nach klimafreundlich produziertem Stahl angekurbelt werden.
Der Aufbau des Marktes verzögere sich gegenüber bisherigen Erwartungen, erklärte das Ministerium. Die Produktionskosten lägen weiterhin deutlich über denen fossiler Alternativen.
Staat will Mehrkosten für Unternehmen ausgleichen
Die zusätzlichen Hilfen für die Industrie sollen im Rahmen sogenannter CO2-Differenzverträge vergeben werden. Damit gleicht der Staat über einen Zeitraum von 15 Jahren Mehrkosten aus, die Unternehmen durch die Umstellung auf klimafreundliche Verfahren entstehen.
In der nächsten Ausschreibungsrunde 2027 soll erstmals ein eigenes Förderbudget für Wasserstoffprojekte mit mindestens 1,5 Milliarden Euro reserviert werden. Bei hoher Nachfrage könne das Volumen aufgestockt werden, hieß es.
Neuer Fahrplan für Kraftwerk-Umrüstungen
Darüber hinaus ist die Förderung von Gaskraftwerken mit einer Gesamtleistung von vier Gigawatt für den späteren Betrieb mit Wasserstoff geplant. Vorgesehen sind Ausschreibungen für zunächst zwei Gigawatt 2027, die ab 2040 mit Wasserstoff laufen sollen. Weitere zwei Gigawatt sollen zwischen 2030 und 2032 ausgeschrieben und ab 2043 umgestellt werden.
Der Staat solle die wirtschaftliche Lücke überbrücken, die durch Umrüstkosten und die höheren Betriebskosten im Vergleich zu Erdgas entstehen würden. Die Details würden derzeit ausgearbeitet, so das Ministerium.
Grüner Stahl soll begünstigt werden
Um die Nachfrage anzukurbeln, will das Ministerium erstmals einen Leitmarkt für klimafreundlich produzierten Stahl schaffen. Bei neuen Ausschreibungen für Offshore-Windparks soll der CO2-Fußabdruck der Anlagen ein Kriterium sein.
Dies soll den Einsatz von Stahl begünstigen, der mit erneuerbarem oder kohlenstoffarmem Wasserstoff hergestellt wird. Auch für die öffentliche Beschaffung von Stahl und Zement strebt die Bundesregierung entsprechende Vorgaben an.
Bessere Produktionsbedingungen für Wasserstoff
Zugleich setzt das Ministerium auf günstigere Produktionsbedingungen und dringt auf eine pragmatische Anpassung der europäischen Vorgaben zur Herstellung von erneuerbarem Wasserstoff. Zudem sollen Elektrolyseure, die Wasserstoff mithilfe von Strom erzeugen, von günstigen Netzentgelten profitieren.
Für bereits weit fortgeschrittene Elektrolyse-Projekte, die bis August 2029 in Betrieb gehen, soll die bisherige Befreiung von Stromnetzentgelten fortgelten.
Schwerpunkt auf Ausbau und Infrastruktur
Ein weiterer Schwerpunkt liegt auf dem Ausbau der Infrastruktur und auf Importen. Nach Ministeriumsangaben sind 2025 bereits mehr als 500 Kilometer des Wasserstoff-Kernnetzes in Betrieb gegangen, weitere 2.200 Kilometer befinden sich in der Realisierung. Bund und Länder wollen für den Aufbau in den kommenden Jahren insgesamt 4,2 Milliarden Euro bereitstellen.
Das Ministerium setzt zugleich auf Importe über Pipelines aus Europa und per Schiff aus anderen Weltregionen. Auch kohlenstoffarmer Wasserstoff soll stärker berücksichtigt werden.

title: Відключення світла 20 жовтня: які графіки діятимуть
content_c:
Відключення світла 20 жовтня: які графіки діятимуть
В Україні запровадять графіки відключення електроенергії 20 жовтня.
В Україні 20 жовтня обмежуватимуть споживання світла. В частині областей для населення діятимуть графіки відключень, а для промисловості обмеження запровадять по всій країні.
Про це повідомили в НЕК «Укренерго».
Відключення світла 20 жовтня — які графіки застосують
У компанії зауважили, що причиною запровадження обмежень стали наслідки масованих російських атак на українські енергооб’єкти.
За інформацією компанії, обмеження діятимуть від 06:00 до 23:59 у таких форматах:
- Для промисловості: графіки обмеження потужності застосують в усіх регіонах України.
- Для всіх категорій споживачів (зокрема населення): у частині областей запровадять графіки погодинних відключень обсягом від 1 до 2 черг.
В «Укренерго» зауважили, що через обстріли ситуація в енергосистемі може змінюватися. Споживачів закликають стежити за оновленнями та точними графіками на офіційних сторінках місцевих обленерго, а також ощадливо використовувати електроенергію, коли з’являється світло.
Відключення світла в Україні — останні новини
Нагадаємо, 19 жовтня у кількох областях обмежать світло для бізнесу та запровадять погодинні графіки відключень. В «Укренерго» пояснили, що це наслідки російських атак на енергетику.
У ніч проти 19 жовтня війська РФ знову вдарили по енергетиці України. Через обстріл частина Вінницької та Рівненської областей залишилася без світла.

title: Трамп призвал переименовать штат Нью-Мексико в «Нью-Америка»
content_c:
Президент США Дональд Трамп призвал переименовать штат Нью-Мексико в «Нью-Америка» после своих решений изменить названия Мексиканского залива и озера Онтарио, добавив к ним слово «Америка».
«Нью-Мексико должно немедленно сменить своё название на Нью-Америка. Мы не Мексика, мы — Соединённые Штаты Америки», — написал президент в понедельник в Truth Social.
По мнению Трампа, новое название повысит престиж штата и положительно повлияет на его экономику.
«Это название значительно повысит ценность и престиж штата! Стоимость жилья и доходы вырастут, а вы будете ещё больше гордиться, отдавая честь нашему прекрасному американскому флагу!» — заявил он.
«Возможно, даже фальсифицированные выборы, которыми славится Нью-Мексико, снова станут честными», — добавил президент.
Это уже не первая попытка Трампа поднять вопрос о переименовании штата. В прошлом месяце он опубликовал в Truth Social карту, на которой слово «Мексико» в названии штата было перечеркнуто большим знаком «X», а ниже написано «Америка». Официальный аккаунт Белого дома распространил это изображение в соцсети X.
В Нью-Мексико ответили Трампу: название штата старше самих США
Сенатор-демократ от Нью-Мексико Бен Рэй Лухан написал в соцсетях, что название штата имеет многовековую историю, начавшуюся задолго до образования Соединенных Штатов.
«Название Нью-Мексико существует уже сотни лет, задолго до появления самих Соединённых Штатов. Оно хранит историю многих поколений, культуру и богатые традиции, которые до сих пор формируют нашу идентичность», — отметил сенатор.
«Мы — жители Нью-Мексико. Мы гордимся своим названием, гордимся своим домом и сохраним и то, и другое. Даже когда Дональд Трамп давно покинет свой пост, мы все равно останемся Нью-Мексико», — добавил он.
Трамп хочет переименовывать озёра и океаны
В августе Трамп подписал указ, направленный на переименование озера Онтарио в «Озеро Америка» на фоне торговой войны с Канадой.
Тогда президент народа сенека Джей Конрад Сенека призвал Трампа отменить указ. Он заявил, что переименование нарушает условия Канандайгуского договора 1794 года, в котором границы территории народа сенека определены с использованием формулировки «начиная от озера Онтарио».
Кроме того, на предвыборном митинге в штате Теннесси в начале этого месяца Трамп заявил, что размышляет над переименованием Атлантического или Тихого океана.

title: Зеленський провів онлайн-зустріч із двопартійною та двопалатною делегацією Конгресу США
content_c:
Президент України Володимир Зеленський провів онлайн-зустріч із двопартійною делегацією Сенату та Палати представників США, повідомила його пресслужба.
Глава держави зауважив, що Україна досі стикається з обмеженням швидкості роботи сервісів Starlink і Starshield на різних ділянках фронту.
"Ми досі не маємо пояснень щодо цього. На жаль, лише чуємо різні дивні історії", – зазначив президент.
За словами Зеленського, обмеження швидкості Starlink і Starshield підриває фронтову логістику, українські мідлстрайки та здатність захищатися від "шахедів".
"Найскладніше збивати реактивні "шахеди". Саме тому нам потрібно, щоб Starlink і Starshield працювали на вищих швидкостях", – наголосив президент.
Глава держави зазначив, що атаки Росії стали більш жорстокими та підлими й Україна не отримала від партнерів жодного попередження про першу хвилю балістичних обстрілів минулої ночі.

title: Italy plans tougher security measures after violent protests
content_c:
Italy plans tougher security measures after violent protests
- Published
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is poised to approve emergency security measures, according to local media, after protests over rising costs broke out into violent clashes in Milan.
The measures include extending preventative detention to minors and restricting group gatherings, Milanese paper Corriere della Sera reported.
Police deployed tear gas and water cannons after protesters - many in masks - threw paving stones, bins and chairs at officers over the weekend. More than 250 people were detained, 80% of whom were minors, Italian police said.
The expected crackdown comes after Meloni chaired an emergency security meeting on Monday afternoon. No official announcements have been made.
More than 5,000 people gathered in Milan over the weekend. As well as clashes between police and some protesters, stores were looted and property was set on fire.
High-end shops in the city's centre closed early on Monday, with many boarding up their windows over fears of further damage.
Measures to crack down on youth gangs are expected to be approved as early as Tuesday as part of a decree law, according to Corriere della Sera.
Local media reports suggest social media was used to invite young people to Italy's squares over the weekend.
Rioting and violence have broken out on the sidelines of mostly peaceful youth-led protests in other European countries including France, Spain and Albania, in recent weeks.
Milanese Mayor Giuseppe Sala said he was worried this represented a "new phenomenon" that "originates from an international scenario and therefore feeds itself".
Speaking to Ansa, he said he witnessed "smashed shop windows, looted stores, and frightened citizens", adding that "what happened here is what we are seeing in many cities around the world".
Of the 271 people taken to police stations on Sunday, 32 were arrested, including 23 minors, police said on Monday. A further 28 people were reported to judicial authorities.
Italian media reported that people - including police officers - were injured.
Violence between protesters and police also spread to other cities in the north.
Meloni said people in Turin were detained while "carrying cobblestones and window-breaking hammers", while a train station in Bologna was closed as a precaution after similar disorder.
"To demonstrate is a right. To lay our cities to waste is not," Meloni said on Saturday, adding that "hooligans" had exploited the protests to "sow chaos".
The prime minister - who is facing an election next year - also called on her political opponents to condemn the rioting.
"Do not be ambiguous about this," she said in a post on X, explaining that condemnation must be "unanimous" because "any hesitation becomes justification".
Democratic Party leader Elly Schlein said her party had always condemned violence and that the rioting should not be used to stifle the voices of peaceful protesters across the country who are struggling to make a living, Ansa reported.
The violent disorder followed anti-government protests held by students in various Italian cities on Friday, and echoed similar unrest in neighbouring France, where hundreds of thousands took to the streets.
